docs.text:
350 problems: 282 Medium and 68 Hard. Each lesson includes two or three Python approaches, hints, proofs, and complexity.

Study plan · Template categories · Practice by algorithm

docs.title: Learning roadmap
docs.text:
Complete 80 Core problems before the 270 Extension problems. Within each phase, follow topic and catalog order. The three-digit prefix is the learning step; # identifies the LeetCode problem. Previous/next links follow this same sequence.

At five new problems per week, allow about 16 weeks for Core and 70 for the full path; ten per week gives about 35 weeks. Revisit the same problem with another data structure or algorithm during review.

docs.title: Python interview algorithm templates
docs.text:
Use this as a review sheet before solving a problem. Choose a pattern, state its invariant, then adapt the skeleton to the problem's input and output contract. The roadmap gives the study order; each problem writeup links back to its relevant sections.

Python snippets use standard-library APIs available in Python 3.10+. A name such as Node denotes the node class supplied by the problem; callback parameters such as feasible or neighbors are functions you provide. These are reusable skeletons, so boundary conditions and output shape still need to match the particular problem.

docs.title: Choose a pattern quickly
docs.text: Signal in the question First pattern to consider Question to settle Equal counts, repeated values, grouping Frequency maps Which canonical key represents equivalence? Contiguous sum, negatives allowed Prefix sums Count matches or keep their earliest index? Sorted pair or shrinking endpoints Two pointers Why is the discarded endpoint safe? Longest or shortest contiguous window Sliding windows Is validity monotone when boundaries move? Next greater value, widest height span Monotonic stack Which arrival resolves an old candidate? Maximum of a moving window Monotonic deque Which candidates expire or become dominated? Sorted lookup or monotone feasibility Binary search, answer search What does each bound include? Best few candidates, changing median Heaps, two heaps Which extremum needs fast access? All choices or arrangements Backtracking What state must be undone? Shortest unweighted route, spread by minutes Graph traversal What belongs in the initial BFS frontier? Prerequisites or dependency order Topological sort Which edge points to the dependent item? Undirected connectivity while adding edges Union find Does this edge join different components? Nonnegative weighted shortest route Dijkstra Are old heap entries stale? Overlapping subproblems Linear DP, string DP, interval DP What does one state mean before choosing the recurrence? A small fixed state machine repeated many times Matrix exponentiation Does the same linear transition apply at every step? Repeated range sums with updates Fenwick tree, segment tree Is the operation invertible, and which aggregate must be stored? Static rectangular queries Matrix prefix sums Are query bounds inclusive or half-open? Overlap count or changing active intervals Sweep line, ordered intervals What happens to events at an equal coordinate? Few items or keys but many subsets Bitmask DP, state space search What information makes two visited states different? Longest prefix that is also a suffix Prefix function, Z function Can a previously matched border be reused? Weighted connection cost or critical edges Minimum spanning tree, bridge finding Is the output a minimum connecting forest or an edge whose removal disconnects? Uniform random item without storing every choice Randomized sampling What probability must each occurrence have? Integer conversion or nested expressions Parsing, integer arithmetic What token grammar and integer width apply?

docs.title: Frequency maps
docs.text:
Use a hashable summary as the identity of a group. Counts preserve multiplicity; a set does not. Expected hash-map operations take constant time for bounded-size keys, but constructing or hashing a long key has its own cost.

from collections import defaultdict


def group_lowercase(words):
    groups = defaultdict(list)
    for word in words:
        counts = [0] * 26
        for char in word:
            counts[ord(char) - ord("a")] += 1
        groups[tuple(counts)].append(word)
    return list(groups.values())

Invariant: each bucket contains exactly the words with its count vector. Cost: O(total characters + 26 * word count), plus stored keys and output. Practice: 49 Group Anagrams.

docs.title: Prefix aggregates
docs.text:
When an answer combines everything strictly before and after a position, compute exclusive prefixes and suffixes. The combine operation must have an identity and be associative; it need not have an inverse.

def exclusive_products(nums):
    out = [1] * len(nums)
    prefix = 1
    for i, value in enumerate(nums):
        out[i] = prefix
        prefix *= value
    suffix = 1
    for i in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
        out[i] *= suffix
        suffix *= nums[i]
    return out

Invariant: update the running aggregate after using it, to exclude the current position. O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary state beyond output. Prefix/suffix maxima also give a simple O(n)-space baseline for rain water. Practice: 238 Product of Array Except Self.

docs.title: Hash set runs
docs.text:
For consecutive integer runs, begin only where the predecessor is absent. Otherwise the same long run may be scanned repeatedly.

def longest_run(nums):
    values = set(nums)
    best = 0
    for start in values:
        if start - 1 in values:
            continue
        end = start
        while end in values:
            end += 1
        best = max(best, end - start)
    return best

Invariant: each distinct integer belongs to exactly one scan. Expected O(n) time and O(n) space. Iterate over the set to avoid repeated duplicate starts. Practice: 128 Longest Consecutive Sequence.

docs.title: Prefix sums
docs.text:
For an interval ending at the current prefix p, a target sum k requires an earlier prefix p-k. Negative input values are allowed; monotone-sum window logic is not required.

def count_target_intervals(nums, target):
    seen = {0: 1}
    prefix = answer = 0
    for value in nums:
        prefix += value
        answer += seen.get(prefix - target, 0)
        seen[prefix] = seen.get(prefix, 0) + 1
    return answer

Invariant: seen contains only prefixes before the current endpoint when queried. Expected O(n) time and O(n) space. For a longest zero-sum interval, store the earliest index instead of a frequency, seed 0 at -1, and never overwrite that first index. Convert binary zeros to -1 for equal-zero/one counts. Practice: 560 Subarray Sum Equals K, 525 Contiguous Array.

docs.title: Two pointers
docs.text:
Use ordering to eliminate a whole row or column of pair candidates. For sorted pair sums, a sum below target rules out the current left endpoint.

def sorted_pair(values, target):
    left, right = 0, len(values) - 1
    while left < right:
        total = values[left] + values[right]
        if total == target:
            return left, right
        if total < target:
            left += 1
        else:
            right -= 1
    return None

Invariant: every possible answer still lies between the pointers. O(n) time and O(1) space once sorted. Fix an anchor to extend this to 3Sum; skip repeated anchors and successful endpoint values. For container area, move the shorter height. For trapped water, settle the side with the smaller known boundary maximum. These movement rules require their own elimination argument. Practice: 15 3Sum, 42 Trapping Rain Water.

docs.title: Sliding windows
docs.text:
For longest windows with at most a monotone budget, expand right, then shrink until valid. For shortest windows containing requirements, shrink while valid and record each valid candidate before removing its left character.

def longest_unique(text):
    last = {}
    left = best = 0
    for right, char in enumerate(text):
        left = max(left, last.get(char, -1) + 1)
        last[char] = right
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best

Invariant: this concrete window has no duplicate characters and left never moves backward. Expected O(n) time and O(alphabet size) space. Fixed-size permutations use counts and remove index right-width. Character replacement needs window_length-max_frequency<=k. Minimum cover needs occurrence counts, not just distinct-letter membership. Store result indices and slice at the end. Practice: 3 Longest Substring, 76 Minimum Window Substring.

docs.title: Monotonic deque
docs.text:
Retain decreasing-value candidates for a moving-window maximum. Store indices for expiration; a newer equal-or-larger value dominates an older candidate.

from collections import deque


def window_maximum(nums, width):
    candidates, out = deque(), []
    for right, value in enumerate(nums):
        while candidates and candidates[0] <= right - width:
            candidates.popleft()
        while candidates and nums[candidates[-1]] <= value:
            candidates.pop()
        candidates.append(right)
        if right >= width - 1:
            out.append(nums[candidates[0]])
    return out

Invariant: indices increase and their values decrease; the front is the current maximum. O(n) total time because each index enters and leaves once; O(width) auxiliary space. The width must be valid. Practice: 239 Sliding Window Maximum.

docs.title: Stacks
docs.text:
A stack holds unresolved nested or sequential work. Postfix evaluation consumes the right operand first, then the left operand.

def evaluate_postfix(tokens, operations):
    stack = []
    for token in tokens:
        if token not in operations:
            stack.append(int(token))
            continue
        right, left = stack.pop(), stack.pop()
        stack.append(operations[token](left, right))
    return stack.pop()


def truncate_division(left, right):
    value = abs(left) // abs(right)
    return -value if (left < 0) != (right < 0) else value

Invariant: each stack item is a completed expression waiting to be consumed. O(n) time and O(n) space with bounded numbers. Supply a mapping of the four operators to operations; division by zero is excluded. For MinStack, pair every value with the minimum at that depth so pop restores the old minimum. Practice: 150 Reverse Polish Notation, 155 Min Stack.

docs.title: Monotonic stack
docs.text:
Keep unresolved indices whose values are nonincreasing. A strictly greater incoming value resolves all smaller values on top.

def next_greater_distances(values):
    waiting = []
    out = [0] * len(values)
    for i, value in enumerate(values):
        while waiting and values[waiting[-1]] < value:
            previous = waiting.pop()
            out[previous] = i - previous
        waiting.append(i)
    return out

Invariant: no waiting index has seen a greater value yet. O(n) amortized total time and O(n) space. Equality handling depends on the question's strictness. For histogram rectangles, instead keep (earliest_start,height); a shorter bar closes taller spans, and a virtual zero at the end flushes them. Practice: 739 Daily Temperatures, 84 Largest Rectangle.

docs.title: Greedy ordering
docs.text:
Prove that the chosen next item can replace an optimal solution's next item. For compatible intervals, earliest finishing leaves the most room.

def maximum_compatible(intervals):
    end = float("-inf")
    kept = 0
    for start, finish in sorted(intervals, key=lambda item: item[1]):
        if start >= end:
            end = finish
            kept += 1
    return kept

Invariant: among ways to keep this many intervals, the greedy end is no later. O(n log n) time and O(n) sorting space. Endpoint contact is allowed in this scheduling variant. For car fleets, sort positions front-to-back and create a fleet only when its arrival time is greater than the fleet ahead; compare distance/speed fractions by cross-multiplication. Practice: 435 Non-overlapping Intervals, 853 Car Fleet.

docs.title: Binary search
docs.text:
Choose one bound convention and preserve it. This half-open search finds the first value at least target, including an insertion position equal to len(values).

def lower_bound(values, target):
    left, right = 0, len(values)
    while left < right:
        middle = (left + right) // 2
        if values[middle] < target:
            left = middle + 1
        else:
            right = middle
    return left

Invariant: all indices below left are too small, and all indices at or above right satisfy the predicate. O(log n) time, O(1) space. For rotated arrays, identify the sorted half or compare middle with right; distinct values are needed for the simple rule. For timestamp lookup, use bisect_right then subtract one. The Python bisect documentation defines left/right insertion boundaries; its key parameter is available from 3.10. Practice: 33 Rotated Search, 981 Time Based Store.

docs.title: Binary search on the answer
docs.text:
Search a monotone feasibility predicate when the output is a minimum valid capacity, speed, threshold, or time. Ensure the initial high endpoint is feasible.

def first_feasible(low, high, feasible):
    while low < high:
        middle = (low + high) // 2
        if feasible(middle):
            high = middle
        else:
            low = middle + 1
    return low

Invariant: the first feasible answer remains in the inclusive [low,high] range. Cost is O(predicate_cost * log(search_range+1)); state is O(1) beyond the predicate. For integer ceiling division use (amount+rate-1)//rate when both are positive. Prove monotonicity before applying this skeleton. Practice: 875 Koko Eating Bananas.

docs.title: Binary search partitions
docs.text:
For two sorted arrays, search a cut in the shorter array and derive the other cut from the desired combined left-side size.

def median_partition(a, b):
    if len(a) > len(b):
        a, b = b, a
    m, n = len(a), len(b)
    low, high = 0, m
    while low <= high:
        i = (low + high) // 2
        j = (m + n + 1) // 2 - i
        al = a[i - 1] if i else float("-inf")
        ar = a[i] if i < m else float("inf")
        bl = b[j - 1] if j else float("-inf")
        br = b[j] if j < n else float("inf")
        if al <= br and bl <= ar:
            if (m + n) % 2:
                return max(al, bl)
            return (max(al, bl) + min(ar, br)) / 2
        if al > br:
            high = i - 1
        else:
            low = i + 1

Invariant: left size is fixed; the comparisons locate a cut with every left value at most every right value. Inputs must be sorted and combined length positive. O(log(min(m,n)+1)) time and O(1) space. Practice: 4 Median of Two Sorted Arrays.

docs.title: Intervals
docs.text:
Sorting by start makes only the last merged interval relevant for a union.

def merge_closed(intervals):
    out = []
    for start, end in sorted(intervals):
        if out and start <= out[-1][1]:
            out[-1][1] = max(out[-1][1], end)
        else:
            out.append([start, end])
    return out

Invariant: output covers exactly the processed intervals and has no separate overlapping entries. O(n log n) time and O(n) sorting/output space. For inserting into already sorted disjoint intervals, scan three phases: strictly before, overlapping, strictly after. Confirm whether endpoint contact counts as overlap. Practice: 56 Merge Intervals, 57 Insert Interval.

docs.title: Greedy reach
docs.text:
When reachable indices form a prefix, one farthest boundary summarizes them. For minimum jumps, treat reachable prefixes as compressed BFS layers.

def can_reach(nums):
    farthest = 0
    for i, step in enumerate(nums):
        if i > farthest:
            return False
        farthest = max(farthest, i + step)
    return True


def minimum_jumps(nums):  # Destination is guaranteed reachable.
    jumps = boundary = farthest = 0
    for i in range(len(nums) - 1):
        farthest = max(farthest, i + nums[i])
        if i == boundary:
            jumps += 1
            boundary = farthest
    return jumps

Invariant: only reachable positions extend reach; each completed layer uses one more jump. O(n) time and O(1) space. Exclude the destination from the jumping loop to avoid an extra jump. Practice: 55 Jump Game, 45 Jump Game II.

docs.title: Linked lists
docs.text:
Save a successor before overwriting a link. Dummy predecessors turn head removal and empty output construction into ordinary link operations.

def reverse(head):
    previous = None
    while head:
        following = head.next
        head.next = previous
        previous, head = head, following
    return previous


def remove_nth(head, n, Node):  # n is valid.
    dummy = Node(0, head)
    slow = fast = dummy
    for _ in range(n):
        fast = fast.next
    while fast.next:
        slow, fast = slow.next, fast.next
    slow.next = slow.next.next
    return dummy.next

Reverse invariant: previous is the reversed processed prefix; head begins the remaining original suffix. Gap invariant: fast stays n links ahead of slow. Both take O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space and mutate links. Reordering combines middle detection, detachment, reverse, and alternating merge. Digit addition instead allocates fresh nodes and tracks a carry. Practice: 19 Remove Nth Node, 143 Reorder List.

docs.title: Object copying
docs.text:
Use original object identity as the key, and allocate a copy before traversing edges that can cycle. Values alone are not an identity.

from collections import deque


def clone_graph(start, make_node):
    if start is None:
        return None
    copies = {start: make_node(start.val)}
    queue = deque([start])
    while queue:
        original = queue.popleft()
        for neighbor in original.neighbors:
            if neighbor not in copies:
                copies[neighbor] = make_node(neighbor.val)
                queue.append(neighbor)
            copies[original].neighbors.append(copies[neighbor])
    return copies[start]

Invariant: every discovered original has exactly one allocated copy; copied edges always point to copies. Expected O(V+E) time and O(V) map/queue space, plus output. For random-pointer lists, allocate all copies in one pass and wire next/random through the map in a second pass, with None mapped to None. Practice: 133 Clone Graph, 138 Copy List.

docs.title: Tree traversal
docs.text:
Inorder uses an explicit ancestor stack. Level order uses a queue and freezes its size before processing each depth.

def inorder(root):
    stack = []
    current = root
    while current or stack:
        while current:
            stack.append(current)
            current = current.left
        current = stack.pop()
        yield current
        current = current.right

Invariant: each pop is the next inorder node. O(n) time and O(h) stack space. A strict BST has a strictly increasing inorder sequence; kth-smallest counts pops. Level BFS takes O(n) time and O(width) space; its final node at each level is the right-side view. For LCA, record parent references, collect one target's ancestors, and walk the other upward to its first match. Use identity. Practice: 98 Validate BST, 236 Lowest Common Ancestor.

docs.title: Tree postorder
docs.text:
Compute children before parents. An explicit expanded-state stack avoids recursion limits on skewed trees.

def reduce_tree(root, combine):
    if root is None:
        return None
    values = {}
    stack = [(root, False)]
    while stack:
        node, expanded = stack.pop()
        if expanded:
            values[node] = combine(node.val, values.get(node.left), values.get(node.right))
            continue
        stack.append((node, True))
        if node.right:
            stack.append((node.right, False))
        if node.left:
            stack.append((node.left, False))
    return values[root]

Invariant: both child results exist when combine runs. This general version uses O(n) time and O(n) stored results. For maximum path sum, a complete path may use both child gains, while the gain offered to the parent uses only one. Clamp child gains at zero, but initialize the global answer below all node values. Practice: 124 Maximum Path Sum.

docs.title: Tree construction
docs.text:
Preorder introduces roots; inorder identifies when their left side is finished. Distinct values and consistent traversals make this iterative reconstruction valid.

def from_preorder_inorder(preorder, inorder, Node):
    values = iter(preorder)
    root = Node(next(values))
    stack = [root]
    index = 0
    for value in values:
        parent = stack[-1]
        child = Node(value)
        if parent.val != inorder[index]:
            parent.left = child
        else:
            while stack and stack[-1].val == inorder[index]:
                parent = stack.pop()
                index += 1
            parent.right = child
        stack.append(child)
    return root

Invariant: the stack is the unfinished ancestor path; index is the next inorder node to close. O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary stack, and O(n) new nodes. The input is nonempty. Recursive index-range reconstruction is another option, but recursive slicing adds copying and Python's stack depth can become a limit. Practice: 105 Construct Binary Tree.

docs.title: Tree serialization
docs.text:
Record shape as well as values. Here is a preorder skeleton with explicit null slots; the problem lesson uses a breadth-first format instead.

def encode_tree(root):
    stack, tokens = [root], []
    while stack:
        node = stack.pop()
        if node is None:
            tokens.append("#")
            continue
        tokens.append(str(node.val))
        stack.append(node.right)
        stack.append(node.left)
    return ",".join(tokens)


def decode_tree(data, Node):
    tokens = iter(data.split(","))
    first = next(tokens)
    if first == "#":
        return None
    root = Node(int(first))
    slots = [(root, "right"), (root, "left")]
    for token in tokens:
        parent, side = slots.pop()
        child = None if token == "#" else Node(int(token))
        setattr(parent, side, child)
        if child is not None:
            slots.extend([(child, "right"), (child, "left")])
    return root

Invariant: the next token fills the next preorder child slot. Encode/decode must use the same format, and decoding expects encoder-produced input. O(n) time and O(n) total auxiliary/encoding space with bounded integer values. Null markers distinguish a missing left child from a missing right child. Practice: 297 Serialize and Deserialize.

docs.title: Tries
docs.text:
A node represents one prefix and owns its character edges. A terminal flag distinguishes a complete word from an existing prefix.

class TrieNode:
    def __init__(self):
        self.children = {}
        self.terminal = False


def insert_word(root, word):
    node = root
    for char in word:
        if char not in node.children:
            node.children[char] = TrieNode()
        node = node.children[char]
    node.terminal = True


def find_prefix(root, prefix):
    node = root
    for char in prefix:
        node = node.children.get(char)
        if node is None:
            return None
    return node

Invariant: traversed edges spell exactly the consumed prefix. Expected O(L) time per ordinary operation; total storage is bounded by inserted characters. Exact search requires a terminal node, while startsWith requires only a node. For wildcard dots, carry a frontier and expand all children; a dot consumes exactly one letter. Wildcard search can visit the entire stored trie. Practice: 208 Trie, 211 Word Dictionary.

docs.title: Heaps
docs.text:
Retain the k best candidates and expose the worst retained candidate. Python's heapq uses a min-heap for its ordinary heap operations; negated priorities provide a max-heap on Python 3.10.

from heapq import heapify, heapreplace


def k_largest(values, k):
    heap = values[:k]
    heapify(heap)
    for i in range(k, len(values)):
        if values[i] > heap[0]:
            heapreplace(heap, values[i])
    return heap

Invariant: the heap holds the k largest processed values. Valid k is 1..n. O(n log(k+1)) time and O(k) space; the heap is not fully sorted. For k closest, use negative squared distances so the farthest is the root. For k-way merge, keep one head per stream and replace the popped head with its successor. Add a numeric tie-breaker before nonorderable objects in heap tuples. Practice: 215 Kth Largest, 23 Merge K Lists.

docs.title: Frequency buckets
docs.text:
When frequency is an integer bounded by n, bucket values by that frequency instead of sorting them.

from collections import Counter


def most_frequent(nums, k):
    buckets = [[] for _ in range(len(nums) + 1)]
    for value, frequency in Counter(nums).items():
        buckets[frequency].append(value)
    out = []
    for frequency in range(len(nums), 0, -1):
        out.extend(buckets[frequency])
        if len(out) >= k:
            return out[:k]

Invariant: descending bucket indices mean nonincreasing frequency. Expected O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space, with valid k. Independent bucket lists are required; multiplying a list containing one empty list would alias every bucket. If the cutoff has ties, confirm the contract's tie rule; this collection's selected set is guaranteed unique. Practice: 347 Top K Frequent.

docs.title: Two heaps
docs.text:
Partition a stream into a lower max-heap and an upper min-heap. Keep lower's size equal to upper's or larger by exactly one.

from heapq import heappop, heappush


class RunningMedian:
    def __init__(self):
        self.lower, self.upper = [], []

    def add(self, value):
        heappush(self.lower, -value)
        heappush(self.upper, -heappop(self.lower))
        if len(self.upper) > len(self.lower):
            heappush(self.lower, -heappop(self.upper))

    def median(self):  # At least one value has been added.
        if len(self.lower) > len(self.upper):
            return -self.lower[0]
        return (-self.lower[0] + self.upper[0]) / 2

Invariant: every lower value is at most every upper value, with balanced sizes. Insertion O(log n), median O(1), storage O(n). Negation applies on both reads and moves. Equal values may belong to both heaps. Practice: 295 Median from Stream.

docs.title: LRU cache
docs.text:
Keep direct key lookup and movable recency order. In the standard library, OrderedDict supports moving an existing key to an endpoint and removing the oldest item.

from collections import OrderedDict


class Cache:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.data = OrderedDict()

    def get(self, key):
        if key not in self.data:
            return -1
        self.data.move_to_end(key)
        return self.data[key]

    def put(self, key, value):
        self.data[key] = value
        self.data.move_to_end(key)
        if len(self.data) > self.capacity:
            self.data.popitem(last=False)

Invariant: iteration order is oldest use to newest use. Expected O(1) per operation and O(capacity) storage. Updating a value refreshes recency; misses do not. For a manual implementation, use a dictionary from key to node and a doubly linked list with head/tail sentinels. Get and put detach the node and append it before tail; eviction removes head.next from both structures. Practice: 146 LRU Cache.

docs.title: Backtracking
docs.text:
Enumerate choices when each solution needs its own sequence of decisions. State is local to one path and must be restored after each branch.

def enumerate_paths(state, choices, apply, undo, complete, emit):
    def visit():
        if complete(state):
            emit(state)  # emit must save an independent snapshot.
            return
        for choice in choices(state):
            apply(state, choice)
            visit()
            undo(state, choice)

    visit()

Invariant: state describes exactly the current path, and undo restores the parent state. Cost is the explored search tree plus output-copy work; auxiliary space depends on maximum depth and path state. For combinations use increasing indices; for reusable candidates recurse at the same index. Permutations track unused indices. Grid word search uses path-local cells; queens use occupied columns and both diagonal sets. Repeated states across different paths need care before caching. Practice: 39 Combination Sum, 79 Word Search, 51 N Queens.

docs.title: Graph traversal
docs.text:
BFS finds shortest edge counts in an unweighted graph. Mark a node when it is enqueued so multiple parents cannot enqueue it repeatedly.

from collections import deque


def bfs_distances(starts, neighbors):
    distance = {node: 0 for node in starts}
    queue = deque(distance)
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        for child in neighbors(node):
            if child in distance:
                continue
            distance[child] = distance[node] + 1
            queue.append(child)
    return distance

Invariant: the queue is processed in nondecreasing distance. O(V+E) time and O(V) traversal space for explicitly represented graphs. Seed all sources at distance zero for simultaneous spread. Flood fill counts connected components; reverse a water-flow relation to start from ocean borders. In implicit word graphs, account for string construction and clear processed wildcard buckets. DFS uses a list stack and the same discovery rule, but does not find shortest unweighted distances by first arrival. Practice: 994 Rotting Oranges, 417 Pacific Atlantic, 127 Word Ladder.

docs.title: Topological sort
docs.text:
Kahn's algorithm removes dependency-free vertices. An edge prerequisite->course contributes one incoming dependency to the course.

from collections import deque


def topological_order(adjacency):
    degree = [0] * len(adjacency)
    for children in adjacency:
        for child in children:
            degree[child] += 1
    queue = deque(i for i, count in enumerate(degree) if count == 0)
    order = []
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        order.append(node)
        for child in adjacency[node]:
            degree[child] -= 1
            if degree[child] == 0:
                queue.append(child)
    return order if len(order) == len(adjacency) else []

Invariant: degree counts only incoming edges from unremoved vertices. O(V+E) time and O(V) extra space beyond adjacency. A short result proves a cycle. Initialize isolated vertices too. In a strictly increasing grid graph, edges from lower to higher values cannot cycle; counting frozen BFS layers gives the longest path length. Duplicate edges must be counted and removed consistently. Practice: 210 Course Schedule II, 329 Increasing Matrix Path.

docs.title: Union find
docs.text:
Track components while undirected edges arrive. An edge whose endpoints already share a representative creates a cycle. Choose either union by size (component cardinality) or union by rank (a bound on tree height). Both versions below use iterative path halving and return False when an edge joins vertices that are already connected.

class DisjointSet:
    def __init__(self, count):
        self.parent = list(range(count))
        self.size = [1] * count

    def find(self, node):
        while node != self.parent[node]:
            self.parent[node] = self.parent[self.parent[node]]
            node = self.parent[node]
        return node

    def union(self, a, b):
        a, b = self.find(a), self.find(b)
        if a == b:
            return False
        if self.size[a] < self.size[b]:
            a, b = b, a
        self.parent[b] = a
        self.size[a] += self.size[b]
        return True


class DisjointSetByRank:
    def __init__(self, count):
        self.parent = list(range(count))
        self.rank = [0] * count

    def find(self, node):
        while node != self.parent[node]:
            self.parent[node] = self.parent[self.parent[node]]
            node = self.parent[node]
        return node

    def union(self, a, b):
        a, b = self.find(a), self.find(b)
        if a == b:
            return False
        if self.rank[a] < self.rank[b]:
            a, b = b, a
        self.parent[b] = a
        if self.rank[a] == self.rank[b]:
            self.rank[a] += 1
        return True

Invariant: each parent tree represents one component; only roots own meaningful size values. Path compression plus union by size gives amortized O(alpha(V)) per operation after O(V) initialization, with O(V) storage. Union by rank has the same bounds when combined with path compression. Attach the lower-rank root below the higher-rank root; increment the surviving root's rank only when two distinct roots have equal rank. A duplicate union must not increment rank. Compression can shorten paths, so rank is a historical upper bound on height, not the current height and not the component size. Do not reduce rank during find. Without compression, union by rank alone gives O(log V) worst-case find/union time; the compressed bound is amortized, not constant worst-case time for each call.

Example: union(0,1) makes root 0 rank 1, and union(2,3) makes root 2 rank 1. Then union(0,2) makes root 0 rank 2. Finding 3 shortens its path to root 0, but rank 2 stays unchanged. Use size when you also need component cardinality; rank alone cannot answer that query. This structure answers connectivity, not directed cycle detection or shortest paths. Practice: 684 Redundant Connection.

docs.title: Dijkstra
docs.text:
Use a min-heap of tentative distances for nonnegative weighted edges. A later improvement leaves old heap entries behind; skip those stale entries.

from heapq import heappop, heappush


def shortest_distances(adjacency, start):
    distances = [float("inf")] * len(adjacency)
    distances[start] = 0
    heap = [(0, start)]
    while heap:
        distance, node = heappop(heap)
        if distance != distances[node]:
            continue
        for child, weight in adjacency[node]:
            candidate = distance + weight
            if candidate < distances[child]:
                distances[child] = candidate
                heappush(heap, (candidate, child))
    return distances

Invariant: the next nonstale minimum distance is settled; nonnegative edges cannot create a shorter route through an unsettled larger-distance node. The lazy-heap version takes O(V + E log(E+2)) time and O(V+E) space including heap entries. Infinity identifies unreachable nodes. Zero-weight edges are valid; negative weights invalidate this proof. Practice: 743 Network Delay.

docs.title: Euler trails
docs.text:
When every directed ticket must be used once, find an Euler trail over edges. Hierholzer's algorithm records a vertex only after all its outgoing edges are used.

from collections import defaultdict


def itinerary(tickets, start):
    graph = defaultdict(list)
    for origin, destination in sorted(tickets, reverse=True):
        graph[origin].append(destination)
    stack, reversed_route = [start], []
    while stack:
        node = stack[-1]
        if graph[node]:
            stack.append(graph[node].pop())
        else:
            reversed_route.append(stack.pop())
    return reversed_route[::-1]

Invariant: exhausted walks are spliced into the final edge-using trail by reverse postorder. The input must promise an Euler trail from start. Reverse-sorted destination lists pop the lexicographically smallest edge first; postorder handles dead ends that a direct greedy output would mishandle. O(E log E) sorting time, O(E) traversal time and storage. Use lists, so repeated tickets remain edges. Practice: 332 Reconstruct Itinerary.

docs.title: Linear DP
docs.text:
Define what one prefix or total represents before writing a transition. Only discard older states when all dependencies are accounted for.

def nonadjacent_maximum(values):
    two_back = one_back = 0
    for value in values:
        two_back, one_back = one_back, max(one_back, two_back + value)
    return one_back


def minimum_coins(coins, amount):
    impossible = amount + 1
    dp = [0] + [impossible] * amount
    for total in range(1, amount + 1):
        for coin in coins:
            if coin <= total:
                dp[total] = min(dp[total], dp[total - coin] + 1)
    return -1 if dp[amount] > amount else dp[amount]

Robber invariant: one_back is the best processed prefix and two_back is the previous prefix. O(n) time, O(1) space. Coin invariant: dp[total] is the minimum count for exactly total; positive coins make earlier totals sufficient. O(amount * coin_count) time and O(amount) space. For circular robbery exclude one endpoint in each of two linear runs. Word Break uses reachable prefix lengths: a reachable start plus a dictionary substring makes its end reachable. If substring lengths are bounded by L, direct Python slicing/hash checks cost up to O(n * L^2), not just O(nL). Practice: 198 House Robber, 322 Coin Change, 139 Word Break.

docs.title: LIS
docs.text:
Maintain the smallest achievable last value for each increasing subsequence length. Binary search where a new value can replace or extend those tails.

from bisect import bisect_left


def increasing_length(values):
    tails = []
    for value in values:
        index = bisect_left(tails, value)
        if index == len(tails):
            tails.append(value)
        else:
            tails[index] = value
    return len(tails)

Invariant: tails[i] is the smallest possible ending value for length i+1. O(n log n) time and O(n) space. bisect_left gives strict increase; bisect_right would allow equal values. The tails list gives the correct length, but is not necessarily one actual subsequence; reconstruction requires predecessors. Practice: 300 Longest Increasing Subsequence.

docs.title: Grid DP
docs.text:
For right/down movement, each cell depends only on its top and left neighbors. A one-row array keeps the old top and the newly computed left.

def count_grid_paths(rows, cols):
    dp = [1] * cols
    for _ in range(1, rows):
        for col in range(1, cols):
            dp[col] += dp[col - 1]
    return dp[-1]


def minimum_grid_cost(grid):
    cols = len(grid[0])
    dp = [float("inf")] * cols
    dp[0] = 0
    for row in grid:
        for col, cost in enumerate(row):
            left = dp[col - 1] if col else float("inf")
            dp[col] = cost + min(dp[col], left)
    return dp[-1]

Invariant: before updating a column, dp[col] is its top result; afterward it is the current cell result. Both use O(rows * cols) time and O(cols) auxiliary space and require a nonempty grid. Counts combine by addition; costs combine by minimum then add the current value. Initialize the starting cell only once. Practice: 62 Unique Paths, 64 Minimum Path Sum.

docs.title: String DP
docs.text:
Use prefix lengths as coordinates. A compressed row needs the previous diagonal saved before its current cell is overwritten.

def edit_distance(a, b):
    dp = list(range(len(b) + 1))
    for i, char_a in enumerate(a, 1):
        diagonal, dp[0] = dp[0], i
        for j, char_b in enumerate(b, 1):
            above = dp[j]
            if char_a == char_b:
                dp[j] = diagonal
            else:
                dp[j] = 1 + min(above, dp[j - 1], diagonal)
            diagonal = above
    return dp[-1]

Invariant: above belongs to the previous row, left to the current row, and diagonal to the previous row and column. O(mn) time and O(n) space here.

Problem State and transition Initialization or direction LCS D[i][j] is the best length for two prefixes. Equal letters use diagonal+1; otherwise max(top,left). Empty-prefix length 0; scan left-to-right with saved diagonal. Edit distance D[i][j] is minimum edits for two prefixes. Mismatch uses 1+min(delete,insert,replace). D[i][0]=i and D[0][j]=j. Interleaving D[i][j] says the first i+j target characters can consume i and j source characters. Take a matching character from either source. D[0][0]=True; reject unequal total lengths; preserve order in each source. Distinct subsequences D[i][j] counts ways to make target prefix j from source prefix i. Skip source, plus take it when letters match. Empty target has one way; update compressed j right-to-left to avoid reusing a source character. Regex matching D[i][j] means full prefix match. An ordinary atom uses a matching diagonal; atom-star either skips two pattern symbols or takes another matching source character from top. D[0][0]=True; empty input can match successive atom-star pairs. Star modifies the prior atom, and matching covers the whole string.

All five take O(mn) time using their prefix dimensions. Full tables use O(mn) space; the collection's row-compressed versions use O(n). For regex, dot consumes one character and star is not the same wildcard as Word Dictionary's dot. Practice: 72 Edit Distance, 115 Distinct Subsequences, 10 Regex Matching.

docs.title: Interval DP
docs.text:
Choose the last action in an interval when choosing the first would change its neighbors. Open endpoints remain fixed until every interior item is removed.

def balloon_score(nums):
    values = [1, *nums, 1]
    size = len(values)
    dp = [[0] * size for _ in range(size)]
    for gap in range(2, size):
        for left in range(size - gap):
            right = left + gap
            dp[left][right] = max(
                dp[left][last] + dp[last][right] + values[left] * values[last] * values[right]
                for last in range(left + 1, right)
            )
    return dp[0][-1]

Invariant: smaller open intervals are complete before a larger one. If last is burst last, its neighbors are exactly the fixed endpoints, so the two remaining intervals are independent. O(n^3) time and O(n^2) space. Sentinel ones model outside boundaries; do not count them as balloons. Practice: 312 Burst Balloons.

docs.title: State machine DP
docs.text:
When actions change a finite status, name each allowed status explicitly. For at most two stock transactions, track first buy/sell and second buy/sell.

def two_transaction_profit(prices):
    buy1 = buy2 = float("-inf")
    sell1 = sell2 = 0
    for price in prices:
        buy1, sell1, buy2, sell2 = (
            max(buy1, -price),
            max(sell1, buy1 + price),
            max(buy2, sell1 - price),
            max(sell2, buy2 + price),
        )
    return sell2

Invariant: each state is the best cash balance achievable in that status after the processed days. Tuple assignment reads previous-day values for all transitions. Sell states start at zero to allow fewer than two transactions; buy states start unreachable. O(n) time and O(1) space. Never hold more than one stock at a time. Practice: 123 Stock III.

docs.title: Matrix simulation
docs.text:
Write the coordinate mapping before moving values. A clockwise square rotation maps (row,col) to (col,n-1-row); transpose followed by row reversal implements it.

def rotate_clockwise(matrix):
    size = len(matrix)
    for row in range(size):
        for col in range(row + 1, size):
            matrix[row][col], matrix[col][row] = matrix[col][row], matrix[row][col]
    for row in matrix:
        row.reverse()

O(n^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space; this mutates a square matrix. Layer cycles are a second in-place implementation. Spiral traversal maintains four boundaries and checks that each remaining row/column still exists before consuming it. For simultaneous updates such as Game of Life, read the original state from a separate board or encode old/new states in different bits before the final pass. Practice: 48 Rotate Image, 289 Game of Life.

docs.title: Matrix prefix sums
docs.text:
An extra zero row and column let every rectangular sum use the same formula. Use half-open query boundaries to make sizes and empty prefixes explicit.

def matrix_prefix(grid):
    rows, cols = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    prefix = [[0] * (cols + 1) for _ in range(rows + 1)]
    for row in range(rows):
        for col in range(cols):
            prefix[row + 1][col + 1] = (
                grid[row][col] + prefix[row][col + 1] + prefix[row + 1][col] - prefix[row][col]
            )
    return prefix


def rectangle_sum(prefix, top, left, bottom, right):
    return prefix[bottom][right] - prefix[top][right] - prefix[bottom][left] + prefix[top][left]

Invariant: prefix[r][c] sums the first r rows and the first c columns. Construction takes O(rows*cols) time/space; each valid rectangle query takes O(1). For target-sum submatrices, fix two row boundaries, compress column totals, and apply the one-dimensional prefix-frequency method. Practice: 304 Range Sum 2D, 1074 Target-Sum Submatrices.

docs.title: Bit manipulation
docs.text:
State the word width and signed interpretation. Python integers do not overflow at 32 bits, so signed-word algorithms must mask intermediate states explicitly.

def signed_word_add(a, b, width=32):
    mask = (1 << width) - 1
    a, b = a & mask, b & mask
    while b:
        a, b = (a ^ b) & mask, ((a & b) << 1) & mask
    sign = 1 << (width - 1)
    return a if a < sign else a - (1 << width)

XOR is the sum without carries; AND shifted left is the carry. The loop takes O(width) bounded-word operations and O(1) word storage. For a single isolated set bit use value & -value. For a range AND, retain only the common high prefix. For two unique values among pairs, XOR all values and use one differing bit to partition the two singletons. Arbitrary large-integer operations have bit costs. Practice: 371 Sum of Two Integers, 260 Single Number III.

docs.title: Integer arithmetic
docs.text:
Reduce a large exponent by squaring rather than repeating one multiplication for every unit of the exponent.

def nonnegative_power(base, exponent):
    result = 1
    while exponent:
        if exponent & 1:
            result *= base
        base *= base
        exponent >>= 1
    return result

Invariant: result times base raised to the remaining exponent equals the target. O(log(exponent+1)) arithmetic operations and O(1) auxiliary variables for a nonnegative integer exponent. Negative exponents use a reciprocal when permitted. Exact integer division can instead subtract shifted divisors; truncation toward zero needs sign restoration. For factorial trailing zeros, count factors of five with floor(n/5)+floor(n/25)+...; multiplying the factorial is unnecessary. Practice: 50 Pow, 172 Factorial Trailing Zeroes.

docs.title: Fenwick tree
docs.text:
A Fenwick node at one-based index i summarizes the interval of length i & -i ending at i. Updates climb through containing intervals; prefix queries remove the last covered interval.

class Fenwick:
    def __init__(self, size):
        self.tree = [0] * (size + 1)

    def add(self, index, delta):  # 1 <= index < len(tree)
        while index < len(self.tree):
            self.tree[index] += delta
            index += index & -index

    def prefix(self, index):  # Sum of positions 1..index; index 0 is valid.
        total = 0
        while index:
            total += self.tree[index]
            index -= index & -index
        return total

O(log n) per update/query and O(n) storage. A range sum is prefix(right) minus prefix(left-1). Use coordinate compression when indices are arbitrary values; compression preserves order, not distances. Counting strictly smaller values queries rank-1 before inserting the current rank. Updating index zero is invalid. Practice: 307 Mutable Range Sum, 315 Count Smaller.

docs.title: Segment tree
docs.text:
Store an associative aggregate for each interval. This iterative sum tree uses leaves at indices n..2n and half-open query ranges.

class SumTree:
    def __init__(self, values):
        self.size = len(values)
        self.tree = [0] * self.size + list(values)
        for node in range(self.size - 1, 0, -1):
            self.tree[node] = self.tree[2 * node] + self.tree[2 * node + 1]

    def assign(self, index, value):
        node = index + self.size
        self.tree[node] = value
        while node > 1:
            node //= 2
            self.tree[node] = self.tree[2 * node] + self.tree[2 * node + 1]

    def query(self, left, right):
        left, right = left + self.size, right + self.size
        total = 0
        while left < right:
            if left & 1:
                total += self.tree[left]
                left += 1
            if right & 1:
                right -= 1
                total += self.tree[right]
            left //= 2
            right //= 2
        return total

For a nonempty input: O(n) construction/storage and O(log n) update/query. Every tree entry remains the sum of its children. Range-add/range-maximum problems need a different aggregate and lazy propagation; an enormous coordinate domain can use dynamically allocated nodes rather than a full domain array. Practice: 307 Mutable Range Sum, 732 My Calendar III.

docs.title: Sweep line
docs.text:
Convert intervals into start/end events and process coordinates in order. For half-open intervals, combine all changes at the same coordinate before observing the active count.

from collections import defaultdict


def peak_overlap(intervals):
    changes = defaultdict(int)
    for start, end in intervals:
        changes[start] += 1
        changes[end] -= 1
    active = peak = 0
    for position in sorted(changes):
        active += changes[position]
        peak = max(peak, active)
    return peak

Invariant: active is the number of intervals covering the next coordinate span. O(n log n) time and O(n) space. A skyline needs the largest active height rather than the count; a heap with expiry or divide-and-conquer can maintain that state. Process equal x-coordinates together so output cannot contain false intermediate height changes. Practice: 218 Skyline, 731 My Calendar II.

docs.title: Ordered intervals
docs.text:
When non-overlapping half-open intervals remain sorted, only the insertion position's predecessor and successor can conflict with a proposed booking.

from bisect import bisect_left


def book_disjoint(events, start, end):
    index = bisect_left(events, (start, end))
    if index and events[index - 1][1] > start:
        return False
    if index < len(events) and events[index][0] < end:
        return False
    events.insert(index, (start, end))
    return True

Invariant: events is sorted and disjoint; the input booking has start<end. Search is O(log n), but Python list insertion is O(n); storage is O(n). For closed integer runs, adjacent values should merge, so the rule becomes next_start<=previous_end+1. Do not apply calendar endpoint rules to integer-run summaries without adjusting that relation. Practice: 729 My Calendar I, 352 Disjoint Intervals.

docs.title: Merge sort counting
docs.text:
Sorted halves allow a monotone scan of cross-half relationships while merging. This skeleton counts inversions without changing its input.

def inversion_count(values):
    def visit(items):
        if len(items) < 2:
            return items[:], 0
        middle = len(items) // 2
        left, first = visit(items[:middle])
        right, second = visit(items[middle:])
        merged = []
        i = j = 0
        count = first + second
        while i < len(left) and j < len(right):
            if left[i] <= right[j]:
                merged.append(left[i])
                i += 1
            else:
                count += len(left) - i
                merged.append(right[j])
                j += 1
        merged.extend(left[i:])
        merged.extend(right[j:])
        return merged, count

    return visit(values)[1]

O(n log n) time and O(n) peak auxiliary storage. Each strict inversion crossing the split is counted exactly when its right value is merged before larger left values. For range-sum counts, sort prefix sums and maintain two monotone bounds for lower<=right_prefix-left_prefix<=upper. Retain original indices when output belongs to individual array positions. Practice: 315 Count Smaller, 327 Count of Range Sum.

docs.title: Bitmask DP
docs.text:
When there are few items, a mask records exactly which ones have been used. For equal-sum grouping of positive values, the used mask determines the current bucket remainder.

def equal_sum_groups(values, groups):
    total = sum(values)
    if total % groups:
        return False
    target = total // groups
    remainder = [-1] * (1 << len(values))
    remainder[0] = 0
    for mask in range(1 << len(values)):
        if remainder[mask] < 0:
            continue
        for index, value in enumerate(values):
            if mask & (1 << index) or remainder[mask] + value > target:
                continue
            following = mask | (1 << index)
            remainder[following] = (remainder[mask] + value) % target
    return remainder[-1] == 0

Invariant: a reachable mask fills complete buckets plus the stored remainder. Values and group count must be positive, making target positive when divisible. O(n * 2^n) time and O(2^n) space. A mask is exact item identity, so duplicates at different indices remain separate items. For subset-sum feasibility, a Python integer bitset is another representation: bits |= bits << value, with cost depending on the bitset length. Practice: 698 Equal-Sum Subsets, 416 Equal Subset Sum.

docs.title: Minimum spanning tree
docs.text:
Connect all vertices with minimum total edge weight. Sort edges by weight and accept only edges joining different components.

def spanning_tree_cost(vertex_count, weighted_edges, components):
    # components is a fresh DisjointSet(vertex_count).
    total = used = 0
    for weight, a, b in sorted(weighted_edges):
        if components.union(a, b):
            total += weight
            used += 1
    return total if used == vertex_count - 1 else None

Invariant: the selected edges form a forest extendable to a minimum spanning tree; the lightest edge crossing two components is safe by the cut property. O(E log E) sorting time plus near-linear union operations; O(V+E) storage. Prim instead grows one connected frontier. For dense implicit graphs such as all pairwise Manhattan distances, an O(V^2)-time array implementation of Prim uses O(V) state without constructing every edge. Practice: 1584 Connect All Points, 1579 Remove Edges.

docs.title: State space search
docs.text:
A location is not always the full state. Remaining resources, visited vertices, or collected keys can change which moves are possible from that same location.

from collections import deque


def shortest_state_path(starts, neighbors, goal):
    distances = {state: 0 for state in starts}
    queue = deque(distances)
    while queue:
        state = queue.popleft()
        if goal(state):
            return distances[state]
        for following in neighbors(state):
            if following in distances:
                continue
            distances[following] = distances[state] + 1
            queue.append(following)
    return -1

Invariant: each complete state has its shortest unweighted distance on first discovery. With RC cells and K keys, the state bound is O(RC2^K), not O(RC). Use (node,visited_mask) for visiting every vertex and seed every start node when the start is free to choose. A cell-only visited set can discard essential revisits after acquiring a key. Practice: 847 Visit All Nodes, 864 Collect All Keys.

docs.title: Bridge finding
docs.text:
For an undirected simple graph, a DFS tree edge parent->child is a bridge exactly when the child's subtree has no route to the parent or an earlier ancestor. Explicit iterators preserve recursive DFS entry/exit order.

def graph_bridges(adjacency):
    size = len(adjacency)
    entered = [-1] * size
    low = [0] * size
    parent = [-1] * size
    clock = 0
    result = []
    for start in range(size):
        if entered[start] != -1:
            continue
        entered[start] = low[start] = clock
        clock += 1
        stack = [(start, iter(adjacency[start]))]
        while stack:
            node, edges = stack[-1]
            child = next(edges, None)
            if child is None:
                stack.pop()
                above = parent[node]
                if above != -1:
                    if low[node] > entered[above]:
                        result.append((above, node))
                    low[above] = min(low[above], low[node])
                continue
            if child == parent[node]:
                continue
            if entered[child] != -1:
                low[node] = min(low[node], entered[child])
                continue
            parent[child] = node
            entered[child] = low[child] = clock
            clock += 1
            stack.append((child, iter(adjacency[child])))
    return result

Invariant: low[node] is the earliest discovery reachable through its finished DFS subtree plus at most one non-parent back edge. O(V+E) time and O(V) traversal space. This skeleton assumes integer vertices and no parallel edges; multigraphs must identify the parent edge by edge ID. Iteration avoids recursion failure on a 100,000-node chain. Practice: 1192 Critical Connections.

docs.title: Prefix function
docs.text:
The prefix function stores the longest proper prefix that is also a suffix of each processed prefix. Reuse the previous border before trying smaller ones.

def prefix_function(text):
    prefix = [0] * len(text)
    for index in range(1, len(text)):
        length = prefix[index - 1]
        while length and text[index] != text[length]:
            length = prefix[length - 1]
        if text[index] == text[length]:
            length += 1
        prefix[index] = length
    return prefix

Invariant: length is a candidate border of the prefix ending before the new character. Fallback follows already-proved shorter borders. Total time is O(n) because increases and decreases of the candidate length amortize; storage is O(n). For a nonempty string, text[:prefix[-1]] is its longest proper border. Prefix and suffix may overlap. KMP uses the same failure links while scanning a second string. Practice: 1392 Longest Happy Prefix.

docs.title: Z function
docs.text:
For i>0, Z[i] is the common-prefix length between the full string and the suffix starting at i; this convention leaves Z[0]=0. Reuse matches inside the current rightmost known matching interval.

def z_function(text):
    z = [0] * len(text)
    left = right = 0
    for index in range(1, len(text)):
        if index <= right:
            z[index] = min(right - index + 1, z[index - left])
        while index + z[index] < len(text) and text[z[index]] == text[index + z[index]]:
            z[index] += 1
        if index + z[index] - 1 > right:
            left, right = index, index + z[index] - 1
    return z

Invariant: text[left:right+1] matches the same-length prefix and reaches the farthest known right endpoint. New comparisons extend that endpoint, giving O(n) total time and O(n) storage. A proper border begins at i>0 with i+Z[i]==n. Both Z and prefix-function solutions are deterministic, avoiding hash collisions. Practice: 1392 Longest Happy Prefix.

docs.title: Parsing
docs.text:
Separate token consumption from evaluation. A parser's cursor points to the first unconsumed character; every successful token read must advance it.

def read_unsigned(text, index):
    value = 0
    start = index
    while index < len(text) and "0" <= text[index] <= "9":
        value = value * 10 + ord(text[index]) - ord("0")
        index += 1
    if index == start:
        raise ValueError("Expected decimal digits")
    return value, index

Reading L digits takes O(L) arithmetic steps and O(1) auxiliary variables. For atoi, handle initial spaces, optional sign, consecutive digits, then 32-bit clamping. For calculators, define precedence, unary signs, and parentheses before choosing stack evaluation or recursive descent. A flat-expression parser and a parenthesized parser have different grammars. Arbitrary large exact integers add digit/bit costs. Practice: 8 String to Integer, 224 Basic Calculator, 227 Basic Calculator II.

docs.title: Custom sorting
docs.text:
Choose the comparison that corresponds to the output objective. For concatenated numbers, compare a+b with b+a rather than their numeric values or lengths.

from functools import cmp_to_key


def largest_concatenation(values):
    parts = [str(value) for value in values]

    def compare(a, b):
        return (b + a > a + b) - (b + a < a + b)

    parts.sort(key=cmp_to_key(compare))
    return "".join(parts).lstrip("0") or "0"

Invariant: no adjacent pair benefits from reversing its concatenation order. For n strings of maximum length L, comparison sorting costs O(n log n * L) and string storage/output costs O(nL). All-zero input becomes one zero. For two-dimensional envelope LIS, sort width ascending and equal-width heights descending before strict LIS; otherwise equal widths can incorrectly nest. Practice: 179 Largest Number, 354 Russian Doll Envelopes.

docs.title: Randomized sampling
docs.text:
Reservoir sampling chooses uniformly among matching items without storing all their positions. The RNG is supplied so tests can control its state.

def reservoir_index(values, target, rng):
    answer = None
    matches = 0
    for index, value in enumerate(values):
        if value != target:
            continue
        matches += 1
        if rng.randrange(matches) == 0:
            answer = index
    return answer

After t matches, each match has probability 1/t: a prior choice survives with (t-1)/t and the new match is chosen with 1/t. O(n) query time and O(1) space. A precomputed position map trades O(n) storage for O(1) sampling queries. Fisher-Yates shuffling chooses uniformly from the remaining prefix at each swap. Randomized sets use a dense array plus index map and swap-delete; duplicate-aware collections need occurrence indices. A valid-value test alone does not prove uniformity; the probability argument is part of correctness. Practice: 398 Random Pick Index, 384 Shuffle an Array.

docs.title: Doubly linked lists
docs.text:
A hash map supplies identity lookup; a doubly linked list supplies O(1) removal and reinsertion at a known node. Head/tail sentinels simplify endpoint updates.

def detach(node):  # A real linked node, not a sentinel.
    node.prev.next = node.next
    node.next.prev = node.prev
    node.prev = node.next = None


def append_before(tail, node):  # node is detached.
    previous = tail.prev
    node.prev, node.next = previous, tail
    previous.next = tail.prev = node

Invariant: every adjacent pair has consistent forward/backward references, and each live map entry refers to exactly one list node. Each move takes O(1). LRU moves successful accesses to the newest endpoint. LFU additionally groups nodes by frequency and applies recency within the smallest-frequency group. Browser history discards the forward branch when visiting from a past page. Practice: 1472 Browser History, 460 LFU Cache.

docs.title: Circular buffers
docs.text:
Store only head and size; derive the next insertion position modulo capacity. This avoids independent head/tail flags representing inconsistent states.

class RingQueue:
    def __init__(self, capacity):
        self.data = [0] * capacity
        self.head = 0
        self.size = 0

    def enqueue(self, value):
        if self.size == len(self.data):
            return False
        index = (self.head + self.size) % len(self.data)
        self.data[index] = value
        self.size += 1
        return True

    def dequeue(self):
        if self.size == 0:
            return False
        self.head = (self.head + 1) % len(self.data)
        self.size -= 1
        return True

    def front(self):
        return self.data[self.head] if self.size else -1

Invariant: 0<=size<=capacity and live entries occupy size consecutive cyclic positions from head. Capacity is positive. Operations take O(1) time; storage is O(capacity). Empty/full depend on size, so equal cyclic indices are unambiguous. Practice: 622 Circular Queue.

docs.title: Matrix exponentiation
docs.text:
Use this when a fixed linear transition updates a small vector of counts and the number of repetitions is large. Define transition[destination][source] as the number of ways to move between those states in one step. The matrix must be square, its size must match counts, steps must be nonnegative, and modulus must be positive.

def advance_states(transition, counts, steps, modulus):
    size = len(counts)
    power = transition
    result = [count % modulus for count in counts]
    while steps:
        if steps & 1:
            result = [
                sum(power[row][col] * result[col] for col in range(size)) % modulus
                for row in range(size)
            ]
        power = [
            [
                sum(power[row][mid] * power[mid][col] for mid in range(size)) % modulus
                for col in range(size)
            ]
            for row in range(size)
        ]
        steps >>= 1
    return result

Invariant: power represents the current power-of-two number of transitions; result has already applied the powers corresponding to consumed set bits. Squaring doubles the represented length, and a set bit applies that block to the current counts. No input list is modified.

For transition=[[1,1],[1,0]], counts=[1,0], and four steps, the result is [5,3], the corresponding adjacent Fibonacci numbers. Zero steps returns the initial vector modulo modulus.

For d states and t>0 steps, time is O(d^3 log(t+1)) and space is O(d^2). Zero steps costs O(d). These are arithmetic-operation bounds; with a fixed modulus and fixed small d, integer sizes remain bounded. Use rolling DP when t is modest: matrix multiplication has a larger constant factor. Ensure the transition direction matches destination rows, and count extensions correctly: a length-one initialization needs n-1 extensions, while an empty initialization needs n.

Practice: 552 Student Attendance Record II and 1220 Count Vowels Permutation.

docs.title: Python costs to remember
docs.text:
• A list append is amortized O(1); removing index 0 shifts elements. Use deque for queue operations at the front.
  • Slicing a string or list copies the slice. Hashing a newly created string also reads its characters. Include those costs in Word Break and Word Ladder.
  • Sorting a copy and Python sorting workspace can use O(n) extra memory.
  • Use a comprehension for independent nested lists. Repeated references to one inner list make table updates affect several rows.
  • Heap entries must remain comparable on ties; put a unique numeric index before a node object. Do not assume heap order is full sorted order.
  • Ordinary dictionaries and sets give expected constant-time lookup for small keys. Store frequencies, first indices, or object identities according to the invariant the problem needs.
  • Integer arithmetic in these analyses uses the usual bounded-number interview model. Very large Python integers have costs proportional to their bit length.
  • Prefer iterative traversal when a valid tree, graph, or grid path can exceed Python's recursion limit. Bounded-depth backtracking can remain recursive.

docs.title: Two-minute interview review
docs.text:
1. Name the input contract, output shape, and any permitted mutation.
  2. Write the meaning of each state, pointer, map entry, or heap.
  3. State why one update preserves that meaning.
  4. Trace the smallest input, duplicates, a boundary answer, and a failure case.
  5. Give time and auxiliary space separately from output space.
  6. Rebuild the skeleton from memory, then use the study routine to review a problem whose invariant you could not explain.

docs.title: Maintaining the collection
docs.text: Start with the README to browse lessons and the specification for the collection's contracts. Use Python 3.10+ and uv. Solutions themselves use only the standard library. Ruff is a locked development tool.

docs.title: Repository layout
docs.text: Path Purpose catalog.json Ordered IDs, verified metadata, topics, tracks, and template links solutions/ Executable Python approaches and original teaching notes writeups/ Generated, independently copyable lesson pages ALGORITHM_TEMPLATES.md Common algorithm skeletons and invariants STUDY_PLAN.md Practice pace, review intervals, and readiness checks scripts/build_guide.py Renders README and writeups from their source data template_categories.json Nine categories with 59 templates and bilingual labels translations/zh-TW/ Complete Traditional Chinese lessons, templates, and documents scripts/build_site.py Builds both languages and learning-path navigation tests/ Behavior, oracle, mutation, node identity, and documentation checks .github/workflows/ci.yml Runs verification on pushes and pull requests

docs.title: Edit and verify
docs.text:
uv sync --locked --group docs
uv run --locked --group docs -m unittest discover -v
uv run --locked ruff check .
uv run --locked ruff format --check .
uv run --locked scripts/build_guide.py --check

Edit explanations in the solution module's docstring. Edit the renderer when changing README layout. Do not hand-edit generated README or writeup pages. After changing source material:

uv run --locked ruff format solutions scripts tests
uv run --locked scripts/build_guide.py

Then run the verification commands above. Commit both the source changes and their generated Markdown so GitHub readers see the current lessons.

docs.title: Add a problem
docs.text:
1. Confirm its official ID, slug, title, Medium/Hard label, and public availability.
  2. Add an ordered catalog record and links to relevant template anchors.
  3. Create solutions/p<ID>_<slug_with_underscores>.py with the six lesson sections: Task, Hints, Approach, Why it works, Walkthrough, and Cost and pitfalls.
  4. Provide two or three independent approach classes. Start each class docstring with Approach:, Time:, and Space: lines. Keep the first class and public methods compatible with LeetCode. Explain each approach's correctness and costs.
  5. Test every approach using tests.helpers.implementations. Cover meaningful boundaries and ownership/mutation requirements. Include an independent small oracle where it can reveal mistakes that examples miss.
  6. Register a new behavior-test module in tests/test_copyable_variants.py so the same cases run against the actual Markdown code blocks. Update collection-size assertions and the study plan when the intended collection grows.
  7. Regenerate, verify, and inspect the resulting lesson.

Avoid reproducing full official problem statements. Write original summaries and link to the official page. Label educational baselines that exceed a required complexity bound. Local tests are not LeetCode submission results.

docs.title: Put this repository on GitHub
docs.text:
The Markdown links and Mermaid mind map work directly in GitHub's repository viewer; no site build or hosting setup is required. Create an empty GitHub repository, then from this directory run the following after reviewing and committing any local edits. Replace OWNER and REPOSITORY with your chosen destination.

git remote add origin https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git
git push -u origin main

Use an empty remote without an automatically generated README to avoid an unrelated initial history. GitHub Actions will run the checks on the first push; subsequent pushes and pull requests run the same workflow. The workflow uses read-only repository permissions and needs no custom secrets.

docs.title: Preview the reading website
docs.text:
uv run --locked --group docs scripts/build_site.py --site-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/
uv run --locked --group docs -m http.server 8000 --directory site --bind 127.0.0.1

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. Rebuild after editing source material. The site adds search, topic navigation, expandable solutions, code copying, and Mermaid diagrams. The language selector preserves the current page. The Problems route visits Core before Extension; its step numbers and previous/next links follow that sequence. Practice by algorithm can revisit a problem under different patterns. Template categories provide a focused page for each skeleton and keep the full reference. The local URL override keeps language links on localhost; omit it for deployment. Diagram rendering needs an internet connection to load Mermaid from its CDN. mkdocs.yml owns presentation; scripts/build_site.py derives navigation from catalog.json and stages Markdown without modifying it. .site-docs/ and site/ are disposable build outputs and must not be committed.

Maintain Chinese lesson prose in translations/zh-TW/lessons/<ID>.json. Keep the six English section markers in notes, translate their content, and list approach names and costs in source-class order. Update both languages when teaching content changes. The builder shares code blocks and refuses missing translations. template_notes.json translates prose around shared template code; the category file owns every template's single category and both display names.

docs.title: Publish to GitHub Pages
docs.text:
Source stays in the private yoyocircle/leetcode-qa repository. The current account plan cannot serve Pages from a private repository. The public yoyocircle/leetcode-qa-site repository therefore contains only generated website files and .nojekyll; Pages serves its main branch from /.

After verification, build with uv run --locked --group docs scripts/build_site.py. Copy site/ into a clean checkout of the hosting repository, retain .git, add .nojekyll, review the diff, commit, and push. Never copy the source checkout or personal notes into the hosting repository. Ordinary source pushes only verify; the manual Build reading website workflow also produces a Pages artifact.

Website: https://yoyocircle.github.io/leetcode-qa-site/.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text: Expand the collection to 350 Medium and Hard problems in 35 topics. Preserve the existing 250 problems and their order; append 100 Extension problems in ten new topics. Keep the original 80 as the Core track, with 270 Extension problems. Each topic has ten problems. Derive counts, topic anchors, roadmap grouping, and study pace from the catalog rather than fixed five-problem assumptions. This is a curated learning path, not an exhaustive copy of LeetCode's catalog. Use official problem links and verified public metadata. Write original summaries, examples, hints, explanations, and Python solutions.

docs.title: Data and ownership
docs.text:
• catalog.json owns the ordered problem IDs, official titles, difficulty labels, source URLs, topic definitions, Core/Extension tracks, template links, and metadata verification date.
  • Each solutions/p<ID>_<slug>.py owns a problem's executable implementations and its learning writeup in the module docstring. Solutions use only the Python standard library.
  • scripts/build_guide.py renders the catalog and solution modules into README.md and writeups/. Edit the source modules, then regenerate the reading material.
  • STUDY_PLAN.md owns the study routine and review advice.
  • ALGORITHM_TEMPLATES.md owns a quick-review reference of common interview patterns, Python skeletons, invariants, costs, and mistakes. Every generated problem writeup links directly to its relevant pattern sections.
  • Tests exercise public LeetCode methods and data structure operations, including boundary cases and important mutation and identity requirements.

docs.title: Behavior and invariants
docs.text:
• Exactly 350 unique Medium/Hard problems; no Easy or Premium-only problems.
  • Every problem has two or three complete Python implementations with different algorithm or data-structure choices. Each implementation class has a docstring starting with "Approach:" followed by "Time:" and "Space:" lines. The first such class keeps the original LeetCode API and remains the default solution.
  • Other top-level nodes, imports, and helper classes are shared support for those implementations. No implementation may depend on another implementation class.
  • The renderer makes each implementation separately copyable under the canonical LeetCode class name and shows its name, time, and space in a comparison table.
  • Explain correctness and tradeoffs for every approach. Label educational baselines that miss a required complexity bound; never imply those pass full constraints.
  • Tests exercise every implementation, including public design APIs and boundaries.
  • Preserve LeetCode method signatures and each problem's promised input domain.
  • Each lesson explains the task, hints, approach, correctness, complexity, a worked example, and common mistakes. State input mutation and material Python costs.
  • Local solutions are independent files that can be copied into LeetCode's Python3 editor. Node definitions are included where needed for local execution.
  • Readers can browse by topic and reveal the approach and code after trying hints.
  • The README includes an ordered learning roadmap, a topic mind map, a suggested study pace, Core/Extension choices, and links to all lessons and quick-review templates.
  • Do not claim local tests are actual LeetCode submissions.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: Run standard-library unittest, Ruff formatting and lint, and a generated-content consistency check. Include small exhaustive or seeded oracle comparisons where they add confidence beyond examples. All checks run locally without LeetCode login. Pin development tools in uv.lock. The GitHub Actions workflow runs the same checks on Python 3.10 and 3.12 with read-only repository permissions. Keep generated Markdown in Git so GitHub readers can browse without running a build.

docs.title: Reading website
docs.text:
The reading site has complete English and Traditional Chinese editions. The language selector keeps the current page. Python implementations are shared; translations under translations/zh-TW/ own localized teaching prose and labels. Missing translations fail the build rather than silently displaying English. Keep original repository URLs, catalog order fields, and solution APIs unchanged. The website's primary path visits Core first, then Extension, preserving catalog topic/order within each track. Display learning step numbers separately from LeetCode IDs. Previous/next navigation follows that same path. An algorithm-review index may link the same problem under several patterns; it does not duplicate code. Template categories own one placement for each of the 59 templates. Category pages and per-template pages preserve links from the existing monolithic reference.

Build a static Material for MkDocs site from the existing Markdown and catalog. scripts/build_site.py owns staging and derives navigation from catalog order. Staging in .site-docs/ and HTML in site/ are disposable, ignored outputs. The build must not mutate canonical Markdown. Preserve relative links, template anchors, raw Python downloads, expandable solutions, code copying, search, and the roadmap diagrams under the /leetcode-qa-site/ deployment prefix. Use a strict build and test navigation coverage and disclosure rendering. GitHub Actions verifies builds on pushes. Publication copies generated output to the public hosting repository; the source repository remains private. A manual dispatch builds an artifact for review. Personal-account Pages content is publicly readable; obtain the owner's approval before enabling or dispatching deployment. Private-repository Pages also requires an eligible GitHub plan. Do not change repository visibility to bypass that limit.

docs.title: Compatibility and failure modes
docs.text: All existing 250 default APIs, catalog positions, and source/writeup paths remain compatible. The original 80 Core problems keep their ordering.
