docs.text:
Time: O(R*C)

Space: O(C)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Persistent left and right limits
    Time: O(R*C)
    Space: O(C)
    """

    def maximalRectangle(self, matrix: list[list[str]]) -> int:
        width = len(matrix[0])
        heights, left, right = [0] * width, [0] * width, [width] * width
        answer = 0
        for row in matrix:
            boundary = 0
            for c in range(width):
                if row[c] == "1":
                    heights[c] += 1
                    left[c] = max(left[c], boundary)
                else:
                    heights[c], left[c], right[c], boundary = 0, 0, width, c + 1
            boundary = width
            for c in range(width - 1, -1, -1):
                if row[c] == "1":
                    right[c] = min(right[c], boundary)
                    answer = max(answer, heights[c] * (right[c] - left[c]))
                else:
                    boundary = c
        return answer

docs.title: 1. Two stable linked chains
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(1)

class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


class Solution:
    """Approach: Two stable linked chains
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def partition(self, head: ListNode | None, x: int) -> ListNode | None:
        small = small_tail = ListNode()
        large = large_tail = ListNode()
        while head:
            following = head.next
            if head.val < x:
                small_tail.next = head
                small_tail = head
            else:
                large_tail.next = head
                large_tail = head
            head = following
        large_tail.next = None
        small_tail.next = large.next
        return small.next

docs.title: 2. Stable node-reference partition
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


class Solution:
    """Approach: Stable node-reference partition
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def partition(self, head: ListNode | None, x: int) -> ListNode | None:
        small, large = [], []
        while head:
            (small if head.val < x else large).append(head)
            head = head.next
        ordered = small + large
        for index, node in enumerate(ordered):
            node.next = ordered[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(ordered) else None
        return ordered[0] if ordered else None

docs.title: Bottom-up length and position table

docs.title: Memoized substring-index split states
docs.text: Every recursive scrambling has one top split and one of the two child orders. Testing all splits with recursively valid children is sufficient and necessary; preserving character multiplicities is an additional necessary pruning condition.

docs.title: 1. Memoized substring-index split states
docs.text:
Time: O(n^4)

Space: O(n^3)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Memoized substring-index split states
    Time: O(n^4)
    Space: O(n^3)
    """

    def isScramble(self, s1: str, s2: str) -> bool:
        from functools import cache

        def prefixes(text):
            table = [[0] * 26]
            for character in text:
                row = table[-1].copy()
                row[ord(character) - ord("a")] += 1
                table.append(row)
            return table

        first, second = prefixes(s1), prefixes(s2)

        @cache
        def solve(i, j, length):
            if all(s1[i + offset] == s2[j + offset] for offset in range(length)):
                return True
            if any(
                first[i + length][letter] - first[i][letter]
                != second[j + length][letter] - second[j][letter]
                for letter in range(26)
            ):
                return False
            for cut in range(1, length):
                if solve(i, j, cut) and solve(i + cut, j + cut, length - cut):
                    return True
                if solve(i, j + length - cut, cut) and solve(i + cut, j, length - cut):
                    return True
            return False

        return solve(0, 0, len(s1))

docs.title: 2. Bottom-up length and position table
docs.text:
Time: O(n^4)

Space: O(n^3)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Bottom-up length and position table
    Time: O(n^4)
    Space: O(n^3)
    """

    def isScramble(self, s1: str, s2: str) -> bool:
        n = len(s1)
        dp = [[[False] * n for _ in range(n)] for _ in range(n + 1)]
        for i in range(n):
            for j in range(n):
                dp[1][i][j] = s1[i] == s2[j]
        for length in range(2, n + 1):
            for i in range(n - length + 1):
                for j in range(n - length + 1):
                    dp[length][i][j] = any(
                        (dp[cut][i][j] and dp[length - cut][i + cut][j + cut])
                        or (dp[cut][i][j + length - cut] and dp[length - cut][i + cut][j])
                        for cut in range(1, length)
                    )
        return dp[n][0][0]

docs.title: Depth-local duplicate skipping
docs.text: Sort a copy, record each path, and choose later indices. Skip equal candidates at the same depth while permitting equal values deeper in a path.

docs.title: Extend only the new subset block
docs.text: Start with the empty subset. A new value extends all existing subsets; a repeated value extends only the block created by its immediate predecessor.

docs.title: Depth-local duplicate skipping
docs.text: Every multiset subset has one sorted path. Equal alternatives at a depth generate the same path family and can be skipped without losing different multiplicities.

docs.text: Subsets containing j copies arise by extending those newly created with j-1 copies. Restricting the source block prevents recreating subsets already generated by earlier identical values.

Input is unchanged. Preserve the old result length before appending. Every saved subset must be a fresh list, and output order need not match a particular traversal.

Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output

class Solution:
    """Approach: Depth-local duplicate skipping
    Time: O(n*2^n) loose bound
    Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def subsetsWithDup(self, nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
        values = sorted(nums)
        result, path = [], []

        def visit(start):
            result.append(path.copy())
            for index in range(start, len(values)):
                if index > start and values[index] == values[index - 1]:
                    continue
                path.append(values[index])
                visit(index + 1)
                path.pop()

        visit(0)
        return result

docs.text:
Time: O(n*2^n) loose bound

Space: O(n*2^n) including output

class Solution:
    """Approach: Extend only the new subset block
    Time: O(n*2^n) loose bound
    Space: O(n*2^n) including output
    """

    def subsetsWithDup(self, nums: list[int]) -> list[list[int]]:
        values = sorted(nums)
        result = [[]]
        previous_start = 0
        for index, value in enumerate(values):
            start = previous_start if index and value == values[index - 1] else 0
            previous_start = len(result)
            result.extend(result[position] + [value] for position in range(start, previous_start))
        return result

class Solution:
    """Approach: Rolling prefix decode counts
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def numDecodings(self, s: str) -> int:
        older, previous = 1, int(s[0] != "0")
        for index in range(1, len(s)):
            current = previous if s[index] != "0" else 0
            if s[index - 1] == "1" or (s[index - 1] == "2" and s[index] <= "6"):
                current += older
            older, previous = previous, current
        return previous

Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Memoized suffix decoding
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def numDecodings(self, s: str) -> int:
        from functools import cache

        @cache
        def decode(index):
            if index == len(s):
                return 1
            if s[index] == "0":
                return 0
            answer = decode(index + 1)
            if index + 1 < len(s) and (
                s[index] == "1" or (s[index] == "2" and s[index + 1] <= "6")
            ):
                answer += decode(index + 2)
            return answer

        return decode(0)

docs.title: 1. Front insertion within segment
docs.text:
Time: O(right)

Space: O(1)

class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


class Solution:
    """Approach: Front insertion within segment
    Time: O(right)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def reverseBetween(self, head: ListNode, left: int, right: int) -> ListNode:
        dummy = ListNode(next=head)
        before = dummy
        for _ in range(left - 1):
            before = before.next
        tail = before.next
        for _ in range(right - left):
            moved = tail.next
            tail.next = moved.next
            moved.next = before.next
            before.next = moved
        return dummy.next

docs.title: 2. Reverse reference slice
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


class Solution:
    """Approach: Reverse reference slice
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def reverseBetween(self, head: ListNode, left: int, right: int) -> ListNode:
        order = []
        while head:
            order.append(head)
            head = head.next
        order[left - 1 : right] = order[left - 1 : right][::-1]
        for index, node in enumerate(order):
            node.next = order[index + 1] if index + 1 < len(order) else None
        return order[0]

class Solution:

    Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def restoreIpAddresses(self, s: str) -> list[str]:
        result, path = [], []

        def visit(start):
            missing = 4 - len(path)
            if not missing <= len(s) - start <= 3 * missing:
                return
            if missing == 0:
                result.append(".".join(path))
                return
            for length in range(1, 4):
                piece = s[start : start + length]
                if len(piece) != length or (length > 1 and piece[0] == "0") or int(piece) > 255:
                    continue
                path.append(piece)
                visit(start + length)
                path.pop()

        visit(0)
        return result

docs.text:
Time: O(27*n)

Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output

class Solution:
    """Approach: Enumerate the three cut lengths
    Time: O(27*n)
    Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def restoreIpAddresses(self, s: str) -> list[str]:
        result = []
        for first in range(1, 4):
            for second in range(1, 4):
                for third in range(1, 4):
                    a, b, c = first, first + second, first + second + third
                    pieces = [s[:a], s[a:b], s[b:c], s[c:]]
                    if all(
                        1 <= len(piece) <= 3
                        and (len(piece) == 1 or piece[0] != "0")
                        and int(piece) <= 255
                        for piece in pieces
                    ):
                        result.append(".".join(pieces))
        return result

docs.title: Approach comparison

Approach Time Space Memoized immutable tree shapes O(n*C_n) loose bound O(n*C_n) including output Bottom-up interval tree table O(n^2*C_n) loose bound O(n^2*C_n) loose bound including output

docs.title: Memoized immutable tree shapes
docs.text: Memoize tuples describing every root/left/right choice for an interval. Materialize each final description into entirely new TreeNode objects.

docs.title: Bottom-up interval tree table
docs.text: Fill interval tables from shorter to longer intervals. For each root, clone both chosen subtrees before attaching them to a new node. This uses concrete intermediate trees instead of immutable templates.

docs.title: Memoized immutable tree shapes
docs.text: Every BST has one root and uniquely determined smaller and larger intervals. Their Cartesian product enumerates all valid trees without duplicates; fresh materialization prevents cross-answer aliasing.

docs.title: Bottom-up interval tree table
docs.text: Shorter intervals are complete before use. Combining every possible root and subtree pair gives all trees for the next interval; cloning ensures no returned answers share mutable nodes.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For n=2, the two outputs are root 1 with right child 2, and root 2 with left child 1.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text: Memoized immutable tree shapes: O(nC_n) loose bound time; O(nC_n) including output space. Bottom-up interval tree table: O(n^2C_n) loose bound time; O(n^2C_n) loose bound including output space. C_n is the nth Catalan number. Output itself is exponential and contains n*C_n nodes. Recursion is bounded by n<=8. No caller data is mutated; copying is intentional to keep result ownership independent.

docs.title: 1. Memoized immutable tree shapes
docs.text:
Time: O(n*C_n) loose bound

Space: O(n*C_n) including output

from functools import cache


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Memoized immutable tree shapes
    Time: O(n*C_n) loose bound
    Space: O(n*C_n) including output
    """

    def generateTrees(self, n: int) -> list[TreeNode]:
        @cache
        def shapes(low, high):
            if low > high:
                return (None,)
            return tuple(
                (value, left, right)
                for value in range(low, high + 1)
                for left in shapes(low, value - 1)
                for right in shapes(value + 1, high)
            )

        def materialize(shape):
            if shape is None:
                return None
            value, left, right = shape
            return TreeNode(value, materialize(left), materialize(right))

        return [materialize(shape) for shape in shapes(1, n)]

docs.title: 2. Bottom-up interval tree table
docs.text:
Time: O(n^2*C_n) loose bound

Space: O(n^2*C_n) loose bound including output

from functools import cache


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Bottom-up interval tree table
    Time: O(n^2*C_n) loose bound
    Space: O(n^2*C_n) loose bound including output
    """

    def generateTrees(self, n: int) -> list[TreeNode]:
        def clone(node):
            return TreeNode(node.val, clone(node.left), clone(node.right)) if node else None

        table = {(low, low - 1): [None] for low in range(1, n + 2)}
        for length in range(1, n + 1):
            for low in range(1, n - length + 2):
                high = low + length - 1
                table[low, high] = [
                    TreeNode(value, clone(left), clone(right))
                    for value in range(low, high + 1)
                    for left in table[low, value - 1]
                    for right in table[value + 1, high]
                ]
        return table[1, n]

Approach Time Space Catalan convolution DP O(n^2) O(n) Multiplicative Catalan recurrence O(n) bounded-size arithmetic operations O(1) bounded-size integers

docs.title: Catalan convolution DP
docs.text: Set count[0]=1. For each size, sum count[left_size]*count[right_size] over all root positions.

docs.title: Multiplicative Catalan recurrence
docs.text: Use C_0=1 and C_(i+1)=C_i2(2*i+1)//(i+2). Exact division yields the next Catalan value without storing previous counts.

docs.title: Catalan convolution DP
docs.text: A root partitions a BST into independent left and right subtrees. Different roots or subtree pairs produce different trees, so multiplication within a split and addition across splits are exact.

docs.title: Multiplicative Catalan recurrence
docs.text: The recurrence follows from C_i=binomial(2*i,i)/(i+1). Successive formula ratios simplify to the multiplier used in the loop, so induction yields the same count as the combinatorial recurrence.

An empty subtree contributes one arrangement, not zero. Costs exploit n<=19 and bounded results; for unbounded n, Python integer multiplication and storage grow with the number of bits.

docs.text:
Time: O(n^2)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Catalan convolution DP
    Time: O(n^2)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def numTrees(self, n: int) -> int:
        counts = [0] * (n + 1)
        counts[0] = 1
        for size in range(1, n + 1):
            counts[size] = sum(counts[left] * counts[size - 1 - left] for left in range(size))
        return counts[n]

docs.title: 2. Multiplicative Catalan recurrence
docs.text:
Time: O(n) bounded-size arithmetic operations

Space: O(1) bounded-size integers

class Solution:
    """Approach: Multiplicative Catalan recurrence
    Time: O(n) bounded-size arithmetic operations
    Space: O(1) bounded-size integers
    """

    def numTrees(self, n: int) -> int:
        count = 1
        for index in range(n):
            count = count * 2 * (2 * index + 1) // (index + 2)
        return count

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Rolling interleaving states O(m*n+m+n) O(min(m,n)+1) BFS over consumed-prefix pairs O((m+1)*(n+1)) O((m+1)*(n+1))

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Rolling interleaving states
docs.text: Reject unequal total lengths first. Put the shorter source in columns. Let dp[j] record whether the current prefix of the first source and j characters of the second source form the corresponding target prefix. Initialize the zero-source row by matching the second source alone. For each first-source character, visit columns left to right. A state succeeds through the old state above plus that character, or the updated state to the left plus the second-source character.

docs.title: BFS over consumed-prefix pairs
docs.text: Traverse only reachable consumed-prefix pairs. From (i,j), consume the next matching character of either source; a visited set merges routes reaching the same state.

docs.title: Rolling interleaving states
docs.text: The final target character must come from exactly one source. Removing it gives one of the two smaller prefix states. Each successful transition preserves the source order and matches the target character, hence creates a legal interleaving. Conversely, the final source choice of any legal interleaving is tested. Induction over consumed prefixes proves completeness.

docs.title: BFS over consumed-prefix pairs
docs.text: A transition consumes exactly one source character matching the next target character. Every legal interleaving follows such transitions, and reaching both source ends establishes a complete match.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For sources "ab" and "ac" with target "aabc", consume a from the first, a from the second, b from the first, and c from the second. Repeated a characters make greedy source selection ambiguous; DP retains both possibilities.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text:
For the default Rolling interleaving states approach:

O(m*n+m+n) time and O(min(m,n)) space, including empty-source initialization. Inputs are unchanged. Update left to right and use target index i+j-1. Character counts alone are insufficient because source order also matters.

Rolling interleaving states: O(mn+m+n) time; O(min(m,n)+1) space. BFS over consumed-prefix pairs: O((m+1)(n+1)) time; O((m+1)*(n+1)) space. BFS may avoid unreachable table cells but uses a queue and set. The total-length check is necessary in both models.

docs.text:
Time: O(m*n+m+n)

Space: O(min(m,n)+1)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Rolling interleaving states
    Time: O(m*n+m+n)
    Space: O(min(m,n)+1)
    """

    def isInterleave(self, s1: str, s2: str, s3: str) -> bool:
        if len(s1) + len(s2) != len(s3):
            return False
        if len(s1) < len(s2):
            s1, s2 = s2, s1
        dp = [False] * (len(s2) + 1)
        dp[0] = True
        for column in range(1, len(s2) + 1):
            dp[column] = dp[column - 1] and s2[column - 1] == s3[column - 1]
        for row, first in enumerate(s1, 1):
            dp[0] = dp[0] and first == s3[row - 1]
            for column, second in enumerate(s2, 1):
                target = s3[row + column - 1]
                dp[column] = (dp[column] and first == target) or (
                    dp[column - 1] and second == target
                )
        return dp[-1]

docs.title: 2. BFS over consumed-prefix pairs
docs.text:
Time: O((m+1)*(n+1))

Space: O((m+1)*(n+1))

class Solution:
    """Approach: BFS over consumed-prefix pairs
    Time: O((m+1)*(n+1))
    Space: O((m+1)*(n+1))
    """

    def isInterleave(self, s1: str, s2: str, s3: str) -> bool:
        from collections import deque

        if len(s1) + len(s2) != len(s3):
            return False
        queue = deque([(0, 0)])
        seen = {(0, 0)}
        while queue:
            i, j = queue.popleft()
            if i + j == len(s3):
                return True
            for ni, nj, matches in (
                (i + 1, j, i < len(s1) and s1[i] == s3[i + j]),
                (i, j + 1, j < len(s2) and s2[j] == s3[i + j]),
            ):
                if matches and (ni, nj) not in seen:
                    seen.add((ni, nj))
                    queue.append((ni, nj))
        return False

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Increasing inorder O(n) O(h) Ancestor bounds O(n) O(h)

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Increasing inorder
docs.text: Perform iterative inorder traversal with an explicit stack. Compare each visited value with the previous inorder value; any non-increase makes the tree invalid.

docs.title: Ancestor bounds
docs.text: Carry an open lower and upper bound with each iterative traversal entry. A left child inherits the lower bound and receives its parent as upper bound; a right child receives the symmetric interval.

docs.title: Increasing inorder
docs.text: Inorder lists the entire left subtree, then the node, then its entire right subtree. Strict increase therefore enforces every required ancestor ordering, not just adjacent parent-child relations. Conversely, a valid BST's inorder sequence is strictly increasing.

docs.title: Ancestor bounds
docs.text: Each interval intersects all ancestor restrictions for that subtree. Every node inside its interval satisfies all required ancestor comparisons. A failed strict bound witnesses a BST violation, including duplicate values.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: Root 5 has left child 1 and right child 7, with 7.left=4. Local edges may look plausible, but inorder is [1,5,4,7]. The decrease from 5 to 4 rejects the tree.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text:
Default approach costs and behavior:

O(n) time and O(h) stack space for height h; the tree is unchanged. Equal values are invalid. Iteration avoids recursion failure on a long chain. Use a separate None state for the missing previous value instead of an arbitrary numeric bound.

Alternative tradeoff: O(n) time; O(h) space.

docs.title: 1. Increasing inorder
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(h)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Increasing inorder
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h)
    """

    def isValidBST(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> bool:
        stack = []
        current = root
        previous = None
        while current or stack:
            while current:
                stack.append(current)
                current = current.left
            current = stack.pop()
            if previous is not None and current.val <= previous:
                return False
            previous = current.val
            current = current.right
        return True

docs.title: 2. Ancestor bounds
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(h)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Ancestor bounds
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h)
    """

    def isValidBST(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> bool:
        stack = [(root, float("-inf"), float("inf"))] if root else []
        while stack:
            node, low, high = stack.pop()
            if not low < node.val < high:
                return False
            if node.right:
                stack.append((node.right, node.val, high))
            if node.left:
                stack.append((node.left, low, node.val))
        return True

Approach Time Space Breadth-first levels O(n) O(w) auxiliary; O(n) output Depth-indexed DFS O(n) O(h) auxiliary; O(n) output

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Breadth-first levels
docs.text: Use breadth-first search. At each outer iteration, process exactly the number of nodes currently in the queue. Collect their values and enqueue each left child before its right child.

docs.title: Depth-indexed DFS
docs.text: Walk iteratively with (node,depth) entries. Append a new output row on the first visit to a depth. Push the right child before the left so traversal records each depth left to right.

docs.title: Breadth-first levels
docs.text: Initially the queue contains only the root level. Processing its fixed starting size removes exactly that level and appends exactly the next level in left-to-right order. Induction gives the required grouping at every depth.

docs.title: Depth-indexed DFS
docs.text: DFS still visits all nodes at a fixed depth in left-to-right order when left subtrees precede right subtrees. The explicit depth routes each value to exactly its level without a breadth-first queue.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For root 8 with children 3 and 10, where 3 has right child 6, the successive queue layers are [8], [3,10], and [6]. Return [[8],[3,10],[6]].

Default approach costs and behavior:

O(n) time and O(w) auxiliary queue space for maximum width w, plus O(n) output. The tree is unchanged. Use deque.popleft rather than list.pop(0), which shifts elements. Do not iterate until the queue empties inside a level: children added during that loop belong to the next level.

Alternative tradeoff: O(n) time; O(h) auxiliary; O(n) output space.

docs.title: 1. Breadth-first levels
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(w) auxiliary; O(n) output

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Breadth-first levels
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(w) auxiliary; O(n) output
    """

    def levelOrder(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> list[list[int]]:
        if root is None:
            return []
        queue = deque([root])
        result = []
        while queue:
            level = []
            for _ in range(len(queue)):
                node = queue.popleft()
                level.append(node.val)
                if node.left:
                    queue.append(node.left)
                if node.right:
                    queue.append(node.right)
            result.append(level)
        return result

docs.title: 2. Depth-indexed DFS
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(h) auxiliary; O(n) output

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Depth-indexed DFS
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h) auxiliary; O(n) output
    """

    def levelOrder(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> list[list[int]]:
        result = []
        stack = [(root, 0)] if root else []
        while stack:
            node, depth = stack.pop()
            if depth == len(result):
                result.append([])
            result[depth].append(node.val)
            if node.right:
                stack.append((node.right, depth + 1))
            if node.left:
                stack.append((node.left, depth + 1))
        return result

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Breadth-first alternating rows
docs.text: Process fixed-size queue layers left to right. Reverse the collected values on odd depths; always enqueue left children before right.

docs.title: Depth-indexed DFS
docs.text: Use iterative left-first DFS to append values to depth-indexed rows, then reverse odd rows after traversal.

docs.title: Breadth-first alternating rows
docs.text: BFS supplies each depth in physical left-to-right order. Reversing exactly the odd rows applies the required zigzag without changing later discovery order.

docs.title: Depth-indexed DFS
docs.text: Left-first DFS visits nodes at any fixed depth in left-to-right order. Depth indexing yields the same rows as BFS, and the final reversal provides the alternating direction.

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Breadth-first alternating rows
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(w) auxiliary; O(n) output
    """

    def zigzagLevelOrder(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> list[list[int]]:
        result = []
        queue = deque([root]) if root else deque()
        while queue:
            level = []
            for _ in range(len(queue)):
                node = queue.popleft()
                level.append(node.val)
                if node.left:
                    queue.append(node.left)
                if node.right:
                    queue.append(node.right)
            if len(result) % 2:
                level.reverse()
            result.append(level)
        return result

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Depth-indexed DFS
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h) auxiliary; O(n) output
    """

    def zigzagLevelOrder(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> list[list[int]]:
        result = []
        stack = [(root, 0)] if root else []
        while stack:
            node, depth = stack.pop()
            if depth == len(result):
                result.append([])
            result[depth].append(node.val)
            if node.right:
                stack.append((node.right, depth + 1))
            if node.left:
                stack.append((node.left, depth + 1))
        for depth in range(1, len(result), 2):
            result[depth].reverse()
        return result

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Ancestor-stack reconstruction O(n) O(h) auxiliary; O(n) output Indexed interval tasks O(n) O(n)

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Ancestor-stack reconstruction
docs.text: Use a stack of the current preorder ancestor path and an index into inorder. A new preorder value becomes the top node's left child until that top matches the next inorder value. Pop all matching completed ancestors; attach the new value as the last popped node's right child.

docs.title: Indexed interval tasks
docs.text: Index inorder positions and consume preorder roots using explicit subtree-interval tasks. Each task attaches a new node to a known parent. Push right before left so preorder consumption remains root-left-right.

docs.title: Ancestor-stack reconstruction
docs.text: Preorder fixes the next node to create. Before an ancestor appears in inorder, that next node belongs on its unfinished left descent. Matching inorder values close those left descents; the last closed ancestor is exactly whose right subtree starts next. Distinct values make these matches unambiguous.

docs.title: Indexed interval tasks
docs.text: The next preorder value is the root of the pending subtree. Its inorder index uniquely splits that interval into left and right descendants. Induction on interval size reconstructs the specified tree without recursion or slices.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: Preorder [4,2,3,6], inorder [2,3,4,6]: attach 2 left of 4. Seeing 2 in inorder closes its left side, so 3 becomes its right child. Then 3 and 4 close in order, and 6 becomes 4's right child.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text:
Default approach costs and behavior:

O(n) time and O(h) auxiliary stack space, plus O(n) output nodes. Inputs are unchanged. Each node enters and leaves the stack once. This avoids recursive slices and recursion-depth failures on skewed trees.

Alternative tradeoff: O(n) time; O(n) space.

docs.title: 1. Ancestor-stack reconstruction
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(h) auxiliary; O(n) output

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Ancestor-stack reconstruction
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h) auxiliary; O(n) output
    """

    def buildTree(self, preorder: list[int], inorder: list[int]) -> TreeNode:
        values = iter(preorder)
        root = TreeNode(next(values))
        stack = [root]
        index = 0
        for value in values:
            node = stack[-1]
            child = TreeNode(value)
            if node.val != inorder[index]:
                node.left = child
            else:
                while stack and stack[-1].val == inorder[index]:
                    node = stack.pop()
                    index += 1
                node.right = child
            stack.append(child)
        return root

docs.title: 2. Indexed interval tasks
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Indexed interval tasks
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def buildTree(self, preorder: list[int], inorder: list[int]) -> TreeNode:
        positions = {value: index for index, value in enumerate(inorder)}
        dummy = TreeNode()
        tasks = [(0, len(inorder), dummy, "left")]
        values = iter(preorder)
        while tasks:
            low, high, parent, side = tasks.pop()
            if low == high:
                continue
            node = TreeNode(next(values))
            setattr(parent, side, node)
            middle = positions[node.val]
            tasks.append((middle + 1, high, node, "right"))
            tasks.append((low, middle, node, "left"))
        return dummy.left

docs.title: Inorder simulation by subtree size
docs.text: Count list nodes. Build a balanced left subtree of size n//2, consume the current list value for the root, and build the remaining right subtree.

docs.title: Array snapshot and middle splits
docs.text: Copy list values to an array. Build subtrees using middle indices and interval bounds, without recursively slicing arrays.

docs.title: Inorder simulation by subtree size
docs.text: The left construction consumes exactly the smaller prefix, so the next value is the correct root. Balanced size splitting bounds height, and inorder consumption preserves sorted BST order.

docs.title: 1. Inorder simulation by subtree size
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(log n) auxiliary; O(n) output

class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Inorder simulation by subtree size
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(log n) auxiliary; O(n) output
    """

    def sortedListToBST(self, head: ListNode | None) -> TreeNode | None:
        current, count = head, 0
        while current:
            count += 1
            current = current.next
        current = head

        def build(size):
            nonlocal current
            if size == 0:
                return None
            left = build(size // 2)
            root = TreeNode(current.val)
            current = current.next
            root.left = left
            root.right = build(size - size // 2 - 1)
            return root

        return build(count)

docs.title: 2. Array snapshot and middle splits
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n) auxiliary and output

class ListNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, next=None):
        self.val = val
        self.next = next


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Array snapshot and middle splits
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n) auxiliary and output
    """

    def sortedListToBST(self, head: ListNode | None) -> TreeNode | None:
        values = []
        while head:
            values.append(head.val)
            head = head.next

        def build(low, high):
            if low == high:
                return None
            middle = (low + high) // 2
            return TreeNode(values[middle], build(low, middle), build(middle + 1, high))

        return build(0, len(values))

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Explicit DFS undo frames O(n + output size) O(h) auxiliary plus output Breadth-first sums and parent map O(n + output size) O(n) auxiliary plus output

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Explicit DFS undo frames
docs.text: Use enter and exit frames with a shared path. Entering appends the value and updates the sum; the exit frame removes it after both subtrees finish.

docs.title: Breadth-first sums and parent map
docs.text: BFS tracks cumulative sums and parent identities. For each matching leaf, reconstruct its path by following parents backward, then reverse the collected values.

docs.title: Explicit DFS undo frames
docs.text: The shared path always equals the root-to-current route because each entry has one matching exit. Recording only matching leaves therefore produces exactly the accepted root-to-leaf paths.

docs.title: Breadth-first sums and parent map
docs.text: Each node has one root path, so its parent map and accumulated sum describe that path uniquely. Reconstruction is performed only for leaves that meet the sum condition.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For root 2 with left leaf 5 and right child -1 whose left leaf is 6, target 7 accepts [2,5] and [2,-1,6].

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text: Explicit DFS undo frames: O(n + output size) time; O(h) auxiliary plus output space. Breadth-first sums and parent map: O(n + output size) time; O(n) auxiliary plus output space. The tree is unchanged. Output path copies count toward time and space. Negative values prevent pruning merely because a running sum exceeds the target. Iterative traversal supports skewed trees.

docs.title: Python implementations
docs.text: Each code block is independent and uses the canonical LeetCode class name. Choose one block to paste into the Python3 editor. Shared node definitions are included where needed.

docs.title: 1. Explicit DFS undo frames
docs.text:
Time: O(n + output size)

Space: O(h) auxiliary plus output

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Explicit DFS undo frames
    Time: O(n + output size)
    Space: O(h) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def pathSum(self, root: TreeNode | None, targetSum: int) -> list[list[int]]:
        result, path = [], []
        stack = [(root, 0, False)] if root else []
        while stack:
            node, total, exiting = stack.pop()
            if exiting:
                path.pop()
                continue
            total += node.val
            path.append(node.val)
            stack.append((node, total, True))
            if node.left is None and node.right is None and total == targetSum:
                result.append(path.copy())
            if node.right:
                stack.append((node.right, total, False))
            if node.left:
                stack.append((node.left, total, False))
        return result

docs.title: 2. Breadth-first sums and parent map
docs.text:
Time: O(n + output size)

Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Breadth-first sums and parent map
    Time: O(n + output size)
    Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def pathSum(self, root: TreeNode | None, targetSum: int) -> list[list[int]]:
        if root is None:
            return []
        parents = {root: None}
        queue = deque([(root, root.val)])
        result = []
        while queue:
            node, total = queue.popleft()
            if node.left is None and node.right is None and total == targetSum:
                path, current = [], node
                while current:
                    path.append(current.val)
                    current = parents[current]
                result.append(path[::-1])
            for child in (node.left, node.right):
                if child:
                    parents[child] = node
                    queue.append((child, total + child.val))
        return result

docs.title: Explicit preorder stack
docs.text: Visit nodes using a stack, saving right and left children before changing the previous node's links. Connect each visited node after its predecessor.

docs.title: In-place subtree splicing
docs.text: When a node has a left subtree, attach its original right subtree after the left subtree's rightmost node. Move the left subtree to the right, clear left, and advance right.

docs.title: Explicit preorder stack
docs.text: The stack yields original preorder because children are saved before links change. Connecting consecutive visits realizes the requested chain without losing any subtree.

docs.title: In-place subtree splicing
docs.text: Preorder visits the left subtree before the original right subtree. Splicing preserves that order and moves the next preorder node to the current right link. Each predecessor edge is scanned only a bounded number of times.

The stack variant does not meet the constant-space follow-up; splicing does. Save child references before rewriting links.

docs.title: 1. Explicit preorder stack
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(h)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Explicit preorder stack
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h)
    """

    def flatten(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> None:
        stack = [root] if root else []
        previous = None
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            if node.right:
                stack.append(node.right)
            if node.left:
                stack.append(node.left)
            if previous:
                previous.left = None
                previous.right = node
            previous = node
        if previous:
            previous.left = previous.right = None

docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(1)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: In-place subtree splicing
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def flatten(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> None:
        current = root
        while current:
            if current.left:
                last = current.left
                while last.right:
                    last = last.right
                last.right = current.right
                current.right = current.left
                current.left = None
            current = current.right

Hard · Advanced dynamic programming · Core · Learning step 76 of 350

Official LeetCode statement · All Python implementations · Roadmap

docs.title: Task
docs.text: Count the ways to choose positions from a source string so their characters form a target string in order. Choices with different positions count separately even when the selected characters are identical.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
1. A source character can either be skipped or used for the next target character.
  2. Count target prefixes, and update backward to avoid using a source character twice.
Show approaches, complexity comparison, proofs, and Python solutions

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Backward target-prefix counts O(m*n) additions O(n) integer entries Counts indexed by matching source positions O(m*n) additions O(m) integer entries

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Backward target-prefix counts
docs.text: Let dp[j] count matches of the first j target characters using the processed source prefix. Initialize dp[0]=1: there is one way to choose nothing. All other counts begin at zero. For each source character, scan target positions from right to left. If it matches target[j-1], add dp[j-1] to dp[j]. Otherwise keep the existing count, which represents skipping it.

docs.title: Counts indexed by matching source positions
docs.text: Transpose the counting table: rows consume target characters and columns consume source prefixes. The empty target has one match in every source prefix; a nonempty target has zero matches in an empty source.

docs.title: Backward target-prefix counts
docs.text: Every match either excludes the current source position or includes it. These groups are disjoint. Excluding it preserves the previous count; including it extends any previous match of the target prefix one character shorter, provided the characters agree. Backward updates ensure that both counts refer to the preceding source prefix. Thus each valid position selection is counted once and no source position is reused.

docs.title: Counts indexed by matching source positions
docs.text: At each source endpoint, matches either skip that endpoint or use it to extend a match of the preceding target prefix. These disjoint groups yield current[left]+previous[diagonal].

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For source "aaaa" and target "aa", the count rows are [1,1,0], [1,2,1], [1,3,3], and [1,4,6]. The result is six choices of two positions.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text:
For the default Backward target-prefix counts approach:

O(source_length*target_length) additions and O(target_length) integer entries; inputs are unchanged. Python integers prevent overflow, but intermediate counts can be large, so arithmetic and storage depend on their bit lengths. Left-to-right updates would let one source character contribute multiple times. Deduplicating identical resulting strings would solve a different counting task.

Backward target-prefix counts: O(mn) additions time; O(n) integer entries space. Counts indexed by matching source positions: O(mn) additions time; O(m) integer entries space. The alternate row orientation uses O(source length) storage and forward updates into a fresh row. Intermediate arbitrary-precision counts affect bit cost in both variants.

docs.title: 1. Backward target-prefix counts
docs.text:
Time: O(m*n) additions

Space: O(n) integer entries

class Solution:
    """Approach: Backward target-prefix counts
    Time: O(m*n) additions
    Space: O(n) integer entries
    """

    def numDistinct(self, s: str, t: str) -> int:
        dp = [0] * (len(t) + 1)
        dp[0] = 1
        for character in s:
            for end in range(len(t), 0, -1):
                if character == t[end - 1]:
                    dp[end] += dp[end - 1]
        return dp[-1]

docs.title: 2. Counts indexed by matching source positions
docs.text:
Time: O(m*n) additions

Space: O(m) integer entries

class Solution:
    """Approach: Counts indexed by matching source positions
    Time: O(m*n) additions
    Space: O(m) integer entries
    """

    def numDistinct(self, s: str, t: str) -> int:
        previous = [1] * (len(s) + 1)
        for target in t:
            current = [0] * (len(s) + 1)
            for end, character in enumerate(s, 1):
                current[end] = current[end - 1]
                if character == target:
                    current[end] += previous[end - 1]
            previous = current
        return previous[-1]

docs.text: Walk each level through next pointers already established above. Link a parent's left child to its right, then its right child to the next parent's left child.

docs.title: Perfect-tree neighbor links

docs.title: Breadth-first level linking

docs.title: 1. Perfect-tree neighbor links
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(1)

from collections import deque


class Node:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None, next=None):
        self.val, self.left, self.right, self.next = val, left, right, next


class Solution:
    """Approach: Perfect-tree neighbor links
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def connect(self, root: Node | None) -> Node | None:
        if root is None:
            return None
        root.next = None
        level = root
        while level.left:
            parent = level
            while parent:
                parent.left.next = parent.right
                parent.right.next = parent.next.left if parent.next else None
                parent = parent.next
            level = level.left
        return root

docs.title: 2. Breadth-first level linking
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(w)

from collections import deque


class Node:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None, next=None):
        self.val, self.left, self.right, self.next = val, left, right, next


class Solution:
    """Approach: Breadth-first level linking
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(w)
    """

    def connect(self, root: Node | None) -> Node | None:
        queue = deque([root]) if root else deque()
        while queue:
            previous = None
            for _ in range(len(queue)):
                node = queue.popleft()
                if previous:
                    previous.next = node
                previous = node
                for child in (node.left, node.right):
                    if child:
                        queue.append(child)
            previous.next = None
        return root

from collections import deque


class Node:

class Solution:
    """Approach: Next-level chain builder
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(1)

    def connect(self, root: Node | None) -> Node | None:

                    if child:
                        tail.next = child
                        tail = child
                current = current.next
            tail.next = None
            level = dummy.next
        return root

docs.title: Bottom-up suffix costs
docs.text: Copy the last row, then replace its entries with the best cost from each parent through either child. Scan columns left to right.

docs.title: Top-down prefix frontier
docs.text: Build fresh prefix-cost rows. A cell receives a path from its upper-left or upper-right parent when that parent exists.

docs.title: Bottom-up suffix costs
docs.text: Before overwriting a parent, its two child costs are still available. Every downward path chooses one child, so the smaller optimal child suffix gives the optimal parent suffix.

docs.title: Top-down prefix frontier
docs.text: Every top-down path to a cell ends at one existing parent, so minimizing their prefix costs is exact. The minimum last-row entry selects the cheapest possible endpoint.

N is total entries and h triangle height. Both preserve the nested lists; the first explicitly copies the last row. Negative values are valid because the dependency graph is acyclic.

docs.title: 1. Bottom-up suffix costs
docs.text:
Time: O(N)

Space: O(h)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Bottom-up suffix costs
    Time: O(N)
    Space: O(h)
    """

    def minimumTotal(self, triangle: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        dp = triangle[-1].copy()
        for row in range(len(triangle) - 2, -1, -1):
            for column, value in enumerate(triangle[row]):
                dp[column] = value + min(dp[column], dp[column + 1])
        return dp[0]

docs.title: 2. Top-down prefix frontier
docs.text:
Time: O(N)

Space: O(h)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Top-down prefix frontier
    Time: O(N)
    Space: O(h)
    """

    def minimumTotal(self, triangle: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        previous = [0]
        for row in triangle:
            current = [float("inf")] * len(row)
            for column, value in enumerate(row):
                if column < len(previous):
                    current[column] = min(current[column], previous[column] + value)
                if column:
                    current[column] = min(current[column], previous[column - 1] + value)
            previous = current
        return min(previous)

docs.title: Four cash-balance states
docs.text: Maintain four best cash balances. Initialize sell states to zero and buy states to negative infinity, representing no share held versus impossible holding states before any day. For each price, update in reverse transaction order: second sell, second buy, first sell, first buy. Each transition therefore reads the preceding day's state. Buying subtracts the price; selling adds it. The second sell state is the answer.

docs.title: Best single trade on each side
docs.text: Compute the best one-transaction profit for every prefix. Scan backward while maintaining the best one-transaction suffix profit and combine the prefix/suffix at every split day.

docs.title: Four cash-balance states
docs.text: Every valid action sequence follows the order buy, sell, buy, sell, with optional actions omitted by the at-most-two budget. A state's best balance either comes from taking no action today or from the preceding state plus today's buy or sell. These exhaust all legal transitions. Zero sell-state initialization also permits fewer transactions, and maximizing balances at every stage preserves all future profit possibilities.

docs.title: Best single trade on each side
docs.text: Any two nonoverlapping trades have a split between them. Prefix and suffix optima dominate those two trades, while each combined pair remains legal. Sharing the split day permits selling then buying at the same price without improving beyond valid distinct-day schedules.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For [3,1,4,2,5], buy at 1 and sell at 4 for profit 3, then buy at 2 and sell at 5 for another 3. The final best balance is 6.

O(n) time and O(1) space; input is unchanged. Update backward if the recurrence uses previous-day states. Selecting the two largest individual price rises can produce overlapping transactions. Holding-state balances include purchase cost; they are not realized profits.

Four cash-balance states: O(n) time; O(1) space. Best single trade on each side: O(n) time; O(n) space. The split table uses more memory but separates the two transactions visibly. Neither method sorts or changes the price sequence.

class Solution:
    """Approach: Four cash-balance states
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def maxProfit(self, prices: list[int]) -> int:
        buy1 = buy2 = -float("inf")
        sell1 = sell2 = 0
        for price in prices:
            sell2 = max(sell2, buy2 + price)
            buy2 = max(buy2, sell1 - price)
            sell1 = max(sell1, buy1 + price)
            buy1 = max(buy1, -price)
        return sell2

docs.title: 2. Best single trade on each side
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Best single trade on each side
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def maxProfit(self, prices: list[int]) -> int:
        left = [0] * len(prices)
        minimum = prices[0]
        for index, price in enumerate(prices):
            minimum = min(minimum, price)
            left[index] = max(left[index - 1] if index else 0, price - minimum)
        maximum = prices[-1]
        right = answer = 0
        for index in range(len(prices) - 1, -1, -1):
            maximum = max(maximum, prices[index])
            right = max(right, maximum - prices[index])
            answer = max(answer, left[index] + right)
        return answer

docs.title: Downward gain DP
docs.text: Process nodes in iterative postorder. Save each node's best downward gain. Clamp child gains at zero. Update the global answer with node+left+right, but save only node+max(left,right) as the gain available to its parent.

docs.title: Enumerate all path starts
docs.text: Build undirected tree adjacency, then walk from every starting node while accumulating sums. This directly enumerates all simple paths and is useful as an oracle. Its quadratic time may time out at full constraints.

docs.title: Downward gain DP
docs.text: Every simple path has a unique highest node. At that node it consists of at most one branch from each child, so the global update considers its best form. Returning both branches upward would create a fork, which is not a simple path.

docs.title: Enumerate all path starts
docs.text: A tree has one simple path between each pair of vertices. Traversing from every start therefore considers every nonempty path, while avoiding the previous vertex prevents retracing an edge.

Alternative tradeoff: O(n^2); educational baseline may time out time; O(n) space.

docs.title: 1. Downward gain DP
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Downward gain DP
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def maxPathSum(self, root: TreeNode) -> int:
        gains = {}
        stack = [(root, False)]
        best = float("-inf")
        while stack:
            node, expanded = stack.pop()
            if expanded:
                left = max(0, gains.get(node.left, 0))
                right = max(0, gains.get(node.right, 0))
                best = max(best, node.val + left + right)
                gains[node] = node.val + max(left, right)
                continue
            stack.append((node, True))
            if node.right:
                stack.append((node.right, False))
            if node.left:
                stack.append((node.left, False))
        return int(best)

docs.title: 2. Enumerate all path starts
docs.text:
Time: O(n^2); educational baseline may time out

Space: O(n)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Enumerate all path starts
    Time: O(n^2); educational baseline may time out
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def maxPathSum(self, root: TreeNode) -> int:
        adjacency = {}
        stack = [root]
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            adjacency.setdefault(node, [])
            for child in (node.left, node.right):
                if child:
                    adjacency[node].append(child)
                    adjacency.setdefault(child, []).append(node)
                    stack.append(child)
        best = float("-inf")
        for start in adjacency:
            pending = [(start, None, 0)]
            while pending:
                node, previous, total = pending.pop()
                total += node.val
                best = max(best, total)
                pending.extend(
                    (child, node, total) for child in adjacency[node] if child is not previous
                )
        return int(best)

docs.text:
Time: O(26NL^2 + P*D^2)

Space: O(NL+E+PD^2)

class Solution:
    """Approach: BFS predecessor DAG and iterative reconstruction
    Time: O(26*N*L^2 + P*D^2)
    Space: O(N*L+E+P*D^2)
    """

    def findLadders(self, beginWord: str, endWord: str, wordList: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:
        from collections import deque
        from string import ascii_lowercase

        words = set(wordList)
        if endWord not in words:
            return []
        distance = {beginWord: 0}
        parents = {}
        queue = deque([beginWord])
        while queue:
            word = queue.popleft()
            if endWord in distance and distance[word] >= distance[endWord]:
                continue
            for index in range(len(word)):
                for letter in ascii_lowercase:
                    other = word[:index] + letter + word[index + 1 :]
                    if other not in words:
                        continue
                    if other not in distance:
                        distance[other] = distance[word] + 1
                        queue.append(other)
                    if distance[other] == distance[word] + 1:
                        parents.setdefault(other, []).append(word)
        if endWord not in distance:
            return []
        answers = []
        stack = [(endWord, [endWord])]
        while stack:
            word, path = stack.pop()
            if word == beginWord:
                answers.append(path[::-1])
            else:
                stack.extend((parent, path + [parent]) for parent in parents[word])
        return answers

docs.title: 2. Layered queues of complete partial routes
docs.text:
Time: O(H26L^2 + H*D)

Space: O(HD+NL)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Layered queues of complete partial routes
    Time: O(H*26*L^2 + H*D)
    Space: O(H*D+N*L)
    """

    def findLadders(self, beginWord: str, endWord: str, wordList: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:
        from string import ascii_lowercase

        unused = set(wordList)
        if endWord not in unused:
            return []
        unused.discard(beginWord)
        frontier = [[beginWord]]
        while frontier:
            answers = [path for path in frontier if path[-1] == endWord]
            if answers:
                return answers
            following, discovered = [], set()
            for path in frontier:
                word = path[-1]
                for index in range(len(word)):
                    for letter in ascii_lowercase:
                        other = word[:index] + letter + word[index + 1 :]
                        if other in unused:
                            following.append(path + [other])
                            discovered.add(other)
            unused.difference_update(discovered)
            frontier = following
        return []

docs.title: Wildcard-bucket BFS
docs.text: Build wildcard buckets for the dictionary and start. Breadth-first search stores sequence lengths, initially one. For each pattern of a dequeued word, visit unseen bucket members, then remove that bucket. Reject an absent target.

docs.title: Wildcard-bucket BFS
docs.text: Distinct words share a pattern exactly when they differ only at that position, so buckets supply all valid neighbors. BFS first reaches each word by a shortest sequence. Expanding a bucket discovers all its members at the earliest possible next layer; later scans cannot improve their distances.

docs.title: Bidirectional character-mutation BFS
docs.text: Both frontiers advance by complete unit-distance layers. The first edge joining the two explored layers yields a shortest connecting path. Dictionary removal prevents repeated exploration without removing the opposite frontier meeting test.

Wildcard-bucket BFS: O(NL^2) time; O(NL^2) space. Bidirectional character-mutation BFS: O(26NL^2) time; O(N*L) space. N is dictionary size and L word length. Slicing, concatenation, and hashing each mutation cost O(L); the factor 26 is explicit. Both preserve the original word list.

docs.title: 1. Wildcard-bucket BFS
docs.text:
Time: O(N*L^2)

Space: O(N*L^2)

from collections import defaultdict, deque


class Solution:
    """Approach: Wildcard-bucket BFS
    Time: O(N*L^2)
    Space: O(N*L^2)
    """

    def ladderLength(self, beginWord: str, endWord: str, wordList: list[str]) -> int:
        words = set(wordList)
        if endWord not in words:
            return 0
        words.add(beginWord)
        length = len(beginWord)
        buckets = defaultdict(list)
        for word in words:
            for index in range(length):
                pattern = word[:index] + "*" + word[index + 1 :]
                buckets[pattern].append(word)
        queue = deque([(beginWord, 1)])
        visited = {beginWord}
        while queue:
            word, distance = queue.popleft()
            if word == endWord:
                return distance
            for index in range(length):
                pattern = word[:index] + "*" + word[index + 1 :]
                for neighbor in buckets.pop(pattern, ()):
                    if neighbor not in visited:
                        visited.add(neighbor)
                        queue.append((neighbor, distance + 1))
        return 0

docs.title: 2. Bidirectional character-mutation BFS
docs.text:
Time: O(26NL^2)

Space: O(N*L)

from collections import defaultdict, deque


class Solution:
    """Approach: Bidirectional character-mutation BFS
    Time: O(26*N*L^2)
    Space: O(N*L)
    """

    def ladderLength(self, beginWord: str, endWord: str, wordList: list[str]) -> int:
        from string import ascii_lowercase

        unused = set(wordList)
        if endWord not in unused:
            return 0
        front, back = {beginWord}, {endWord}
        unused.discard(beginWord)
        unused.discard(endWord)
        distance = 1
        while front and back:
            if len(front) > len(back):
                front, back = back, front
            following = set()
            for word in front:
                for index in range(len(word)):
                    for letter in ascii_lowercase:
                        candidate = word[:index] + letter + word[index + 1 :]
                        if candidate in back:
                            return distance + 1
                        if candidate in unused:
                            unused.remove(candidate)
                            following.add(candidate)
            front = following
            distance += 1
        return 0

docs.title: Hash-set run starts
docs.text: Sorting costs O(n log n). Build a set and start a forward scan only from values whose predecessor is absent. Such a value is the beginning of its run.

docs.title: Sort and scan
docs.text: Sort a copy, skip duplicate values, and extend runs when adjacent distinct values differ by one. This misses the mandated linear-time bound but is a useful deterministic baseline.

docs.title: Hash-set run starts
docs.text: Every nonempty run has exactly one smallest value. Only that value starts a scan, so every distinct number is visited within exactly one run. The maximum run length is therefore found without repeated scans.

docs.title: Sort and scan

Expected O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space, using expected constant-time hashing. Inputs are unchanged. Iterate over the set, not the original array: repeated start values in the original could trigger repeated long scans. An empty input returns 0.

class Solution:
    """Approach: Hash-set run starts
    Time: O(n) expected
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def longestConsecutive(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        values = set(nums)
        best = 0
        for value in values:
            if value - 1 in values:
                continue
            end = value
            while end in values:
                end += 1
            best = max(best, end - value)
        return best

docs.text:
Time: O(n log n)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Sort and scan
    Time: O(n log n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def longestConsecutive(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        previous = None
        run = best = 0
        for value in sorted(nums):
            if value == previous:
                continue
            run = run + 1 if previous is not None and value == previous + 1 else 1
            best = max(best, run)
            previous = value
        return best

Approach Time Space Stack of partial numbers O(n) O(h) Morris decimal backtracking O(n) O(1)

docs.title: Stack of partial numbers
docs.text: Traverse with (node,number-before-node) states. Append the current digit and add the number only at leaves. Push each child with that same updated prefix.

docs.title: Morris decimal backtracking
docs.text: Create temporary predecessor threads. Track the current number; on returning through a thread, remove the digits introduced along that completed left descent. Detect its leaf at the predecessor.

docs.title: Stack of partial numbers
docs.text: Induction on depth makes the stored number exactly the path prefix. Every leaf contributes its complete represented number once.

docs.title: Morris decimal backtracking
docs.text: Thread return restores the ancestor context. The counted predecessor-path length tells exactly how many decimal digits to remove. Each original leaf contributes once, and all temporary links are removed.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls

The stated costs use the problem's bounded numerical results; arbitrary unbounded path integers require additional bit-operation costs.

docs.title: 1. Stack of partial numbers
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(h)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Stack of partial numbers
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h)
    """

    def sumNumbers(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> int:
        total = 0
        stack = [(root, 0)] if root else []
        while stack:
            node, prefix = stack.pop()
            number = prefix * 10 + node.val
            if node.left is None and node.right is None:
                total += number
            for child in (node.left, node.right):
                if child:
                    stack.append((child, number))
        return total

docs.title: 2. Morris decimal backtracking
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(1)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Morris decimal backtracking
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def sumNumbers(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> int:
        total = number = 0
        current = root
        while current:
            if current.left:
                predecessor, steps = current.left, 1
                while predecessor.right and predecessor.right is not current:
                    predecessor = predecessor.right
                    steps += 1
                if predecessor.right is None:
                    number = number * 10 + current.val
                    predecessor.right = current
                    current = current.left
                    continue
                if predecessor.left is None:
                    total += number
                for _ in range(steps):
                    number //= 10
                predecessor.right = None
            else:
                number = number * 10 + current.val
                if current.right is None:
                    total += number
            current = current.right
        return total

docs.text: Traverse O cells outward from every boundary O. Change only O cells not in the resulting safe set.

docs.title: Union-find with an exterior sentinel
docs.text: Union adjacent O cells and union boundary O cells with a virtual exterior node. Use size-weighted unions and iterative path compression; flip cells whose root differs from the exterior root.

docs.title: Boundary flood-fill
docs.text: An O region survives exactly when it has an O path to a boundary. Flood-fill finds precisely these paths, so the complement consists exactly of surrounded regions.

docs.title: 1. Boundary flood-fill
docs.text:
Time: O(R*C)

Space: O(R*C)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Boundary flood-fill
    Time: O(R*C)
    Space: O(R*C)
    """

    def solve(self, board: list[list[str]]) -> None:
        rows, columns = len(board), len(board[0])
        safe = set()
        stack = [
            (r, c)
            for r in range(rows)
            for c in range(columns)
            if (r in (0, rows - 1) or c in (0, columns - 1)) and board[r][c] == "O"
        ]
        while stack:
            r, c = stack.pop()
            if (r, c) in safe:
                continue
            safe.add((r, c))
            for nr, nc in ((r - 1, c), (r + 1, c), (r, c - 1), (r, c + 1)):
                if (
                    0 <= nr < rows
                    and 0 <= nc < columns
                    and board[nr][nc] == "O"
                    and (nr, nc) not in safe
                ):
                    stack.append((nr, nc))
        for r in range(rows):
            for c in range(columns):
                if board[r][c] == "O" and (r, c) not in safe:
                    board[r][c] = "X"

docs.title: 2. Union-find with an exterior sentinel
docs.text:
Time: O(RCalpha(R*C))

Space: O(R*C)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Union-find with an exterior sentinel
    Time: O(R*C*alpha(R*C))
    Space: O(R*C)
    """

    def solve(self, board: list[list[str]]) -> None:
        rows, columns = len(board), len(board[0])
        outside = rows * columns
        parent = list(range(outside + 1))
        size = [1] * len(parent)

        def find(node):
            while node != parent[node]:
                parent[node] = parent[parent[node]]
                node = parent[node]
            return node

        def union(a, b):
            a, b = find(a), find(b)
            if a == b:
                return
            if size[a] < size[b]:
                a, b = b, a
            parent[b] = a
            size[a] += size[b]

        for r in range(rows):
            for c in range(columns):
                if board[r][c] != "O":
                    continue
                current = r * columns + c
                if r in (0, rows - 1) or c in (0, columns - 1):
                    union(current, outside)
                for nr, nc in ((r - 1, c), (r, c - 1)):
                    if nr >= 0 and nc >= 0 and board[nr][nc] == "O":
                        union(current, nr * columns + nc)
        root = find(outside)
        for r in range(rows):
            for c in range(columns):
                if board[r][c] == "O" and find(r * columns + c) != root:
                    board[r][c] = "X"

Approach Time Space Palindrome-table backtracking O(n^2 + n*2^n) loose bound O(n^2) auxiliary plus output On-demand palindrome checks O(n^2*2^n) loose bound O(n) auxiliary plus output

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Palindrome-table backtracking
docs.text: Precompute whether every substring is a palindrome using matching endpoints and its interior. Backtrack only through endpoints marked true.

docs.title: On-demand palindrome checks
docs.text: At each start position, test candidate ends using two pointers, then recurse only after a successful test. This avoids the quadratic table but repeats comparisons.

docs.title: Palindrome-table backtracking
docs.text: The recurrence exactly characterizes palindromes. Every partition has one increasing sequence of cut positions; restricting pieces to true table entries enumerates precisely the valid sequences.

docs.title: On-demand palindrome checks
docs.text: The two-pointer test accepts exactly mirrored equal characters. Exploring every accepted next cut covers all valid partitions and excludes any with a nonpalindromic piece.

On-demand palindrome checks: O(n^22^n) loose bound time; O(n) auxiliary plus output space. The string is unchanged. Python substring slices copy characters; all output copies are included in the loose bounds. Recursion is safe for the problem's small maximum string length.

docs.title: 1. Palindrome-table backtracking
docs.text:
Time: O(n^2 + n*2^n) loose bound

Space: O(n^2) auxiliary plus output

class Solution:
    """Approach: Palindrome-table backtracking
    Time: O(n^2 + n*2^n) loose bound
    Space: O(n^2) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def partition(self, s: str) -> list[list[str]]:
        n = len(s)
        palindrome = [[False] * n for _ in range(n)]
        for left in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
            for right in range(left, n):
                palindrome[left][right] = s[left] == s[right] and (
                    right - left < 2 or palindrome[left + 1][right - 1]
                )
        result, path = [], []

        def visit(start):
            if start == n:
                result.append(path.copy())
                return
            for end in range(start, n):
                if palindrome[start][end]:
                    path.append(s[start : end + 1])
                    visit(end + 1)
                    path.pop()

        visit(0)
        return result

docs.title: 2. On-demand palindrome checks
docs.text:
Time: O(n^2*2^n) loose bound

Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output

class Solution:
    """Approach: On-demand palindrome checks
    Time: O(n^2*2^n) loose bound
    Space: O(n) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def partition(self, s: str) -> list[list[str]]:
        result, path = [], []

        def visit(start):
            if start == len(s):
                result.append(path.copy())
                return
            for end in range(start, len(s)):
                left, right = start, end
                while left < right and s[left] == s[right]:
                    left += 1
                    right -= 1
                if left >= right:
                    path.append(s[start : end + 1])
                    visit(end + 1)
                    path.pop()

        visit(0)
        return result

docs.title: Expand centers while relaxing prefix cuts

docs.title: Palindrome table and prefix cuts

docs.title: Expand centers while relaxing prefix cuts

Both preserve the string and use no substring copies. The center version saves quadratic storage; retaining a table may help a later partition reconstruction.
