docs.title: Task
docs.text: Serialize and deserialize a BST into a compact string. Its strict ordering lets the encoding omit explicit missing-child markers.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
1. Preorder plus BST ordering uniquely determines the missing boundaries.
  2. An ancestor stack locates where a new right subtree begins.
Show approaches, complexity comparison, proofs, and Python solutions

Previous: 197 · #337 · Next: 199 · #652

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Preorder values and ancestor stack O(n) O(n) Postorder values and reversed stack O(n) O(n)

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Preorder values and ancestor stack
docs.text: Serialize iterative root-left-right values. Decode in that order: smaller values attach left, while larger values pop completed ancestors before attaching right.

docs.title: Postorder values and reversed stack
docs.text: Serialize iterative left-right-root values. Decode backward, swapping the preorder roles of left and right. Formats are private to each codec.

docs.title: Preorder values and ancestor stack
docs.text: The first value fixes the root; strict BST intervals determine where each later value belongs. Popping smaller ancestors finds exactly the closest ancestor whose right subtree contains the new value.

docs.title: Postorder values and reversed stack
docs.text: Reversed postorder visits root-right-left. Greater values descend right; a smaller value closes completed right ancestors and starts the appropriate left subtree, the symmetric BST construction.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: A BST with root 5 and children 2 and 9 can encode as preorder "5,2,9" or postorder "2,9,5". Each matching decoder restores that shape.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text: Preorder values and ancestor stack: O(n) time; O(n) space. Postorder values and reversed stack: O(n) time; O(n) space. Serialization leaves the input unchanged; deserialization creates fresh nodes. Round-trip with the same variant. Splitting the string and storing values costs linear space. Iteration supports deep BSTs.

docs.title: Python implementations
docs.text: Each code block is independent and uses the canonical LeetCode class name. Choose one block to paste into the Python3 editor. Shared node definitions are included where needed.

docs.title: 1. Preorder values and ancestor stack
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Codec:
    """Approach: Preorder values and ancestor stack
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def serialize(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> str:
        result = []
        stack = [root] if root else []
        while stack:
            node = stack.pop()
            result.append(str(node.val))
            if node.right:
                stack.append(node.right)
            if node.left:
                stack.append(node.left)
        return ",".join(result)

    def deserialize(self, data: str) -> TreeNode | None:
        if not data:
            return None
        values = list(map(int, data.split(",")))
        root = TreeNode(values[0])
        stack = [root]
        for value in values[1:]:
            node = TreeNode(value)
            if value < stack[-1].val:
                stack[-1].left = node
            else:
                parent = stack[-1]
                while stack and value > stack[-1].val:
                    parent = stack.pop()
                parent.right = node
            stack.append(node)
        return root

docs.title: 2. Postorder values and reversed stack
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Codec:
    """Approach: Postorder values and reversed stack
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def serialize(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> str:
        result = []
        stack = [(root, False)] if root else []
        while stack:
            node, expanded = stack.pop()
            if expanded:
                result.append(str(node.val))
            else:
                stack.append((node, True))
                if node.right:
                    stack.append((node.right, False))
                if node.left:
                    stack.append((node.left, False))
        return ",".join(result)

    def deserialize(self, data: str) -> TreeNode | None:
        if not data:
            return None
        values = list(map(int, data.split(",")))
        root = TreeNode(values[-1])
        stack = [root]
        for value in reversed(values[:-1]):
            node = TreeNode(value)
            if value > stack[-1].val:
                stack[-1].right = node
            else:
                parent = stack[-1]
                while stack and value < stack[-1].val:
                    parent = stack.pop()
                parent.left = node
            stack.append(node)
        return root

docs.title: 450 Delete Node in a BST
docs.text:
Medium · Tree construction and tries · Extension · Learning step 124 of 350

Official LeetCode statement · All Python implementations · Roadmap

Quick review: Tree traversal.

docs.title: Task
docs.text: Delete the node with a given key from a BST and return a valid remaining BST. If the key is absent, return the original tree.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
1. One-child deletion simply promotes that child.
  2. For two children, either promote the successor or graft the right tree after the left maximum.
Show approaches, complexity comparison, proofs, and Python solutions

Previous: 123 · #173 · Next: 125 · #654

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Physical successor promotion O(h) O(1) Left-subtree promotion and graft O(h) O(1)

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Physical successor promotion
docs.text: Find the node and its parent iteratively. For two children, detach the smallest right-subtree node and move that original node into the deleted node's position.

docs.title: Left-subtree promotion and graft
docs.text: Promote the target's left subtree when both children exist. Attach the original right subtree as the right child of the left subtree's maximum node.

docs.title: Physical successor promotion
docs.text: The successor exceeds every left value and is no greater than the remaining right values. Its old position has no left child, so detaching it preserves order before it replaces the target.

docs.title: Left-subtree promotion and graft
docs.text: Every right-subtree value exceeds the target and hence every left-subtree value. Grafting at the left maximum preserves all BST bounds and keeps all remaining nodes reachable.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: Deleting 4 from a tree with left leaf 2 and right subtree rooted at 7 with left child 5 can promote 5, or promote 2 and attach the right subtree after it.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text: Physical successor promotion: O(h) time; O(1) space. Left-subtree promotion and graft: O(h) time; O(1) space. Both variants mutate pointers, preserve remaining node identities and values, and avoid recursion. Valid output shape need not be unique. Deleting the root requires returning a possibly different root reference.

docs.title: Python implementations
docs.text: Each code block is independent and uses the canonical LeetCode class name. Choose one block to paste into the Python3 editor. Shared node definitions are included where needed.

docs.title: 1. Physical successor promotion
docs.text:
Time: O(h)

Space: O(1)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Physical successor promotion
    Time: O(h)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def deleteNode(self, root: TreeNode | None, key: int) -> TreeNode | None:
        parent, node = None, root
        while node and node.val != key:
            parent = node
            node = node.left if key < node.val else node.right
        if node is None:
            return root
        if node.left and node.right:
            successor_parent, successor = node, node.right
            while successor.left:
                successor_parent, successor = successor, successor.left
            if successor_parent is not node:
                successor_parent.left = successor.right
                successor.right = node.right
            successor.left = node.left
            replacement = successor
        else:
            replacement = node.left or node.right
        if parent is None:
            return replacement
        if parent.left is node:
            parent.left = replacement
        else:
            parent.right = replacement
        return root

docs.title: 2. Left-subtree promotion and graft
docs.text:
Time: O(h)

Space: O(1)

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Left-subtree promotion and graft
    Time: O(h)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def deleteNode(self, root: TreeNode | None, key: int) -> TreeNode | None:
        dummy = TreeNode(right=root)
        parent, node = dummy, root
        while node and node.val != key:
            parent = node
            node = node.left if key < node.val else node.right
        if node is None:
            return root
        replacement = node.right
        if node.left:
            replacement = node.left
            maximum = replacement
            while maximum.right:
                maximum = maximum.right
            maximum.right = node.right
        if parent.left is node:
            parent.left = replacement
        else:
            parent.right = replacement
        return dummy.right

docs.title: 451 Sort Characters By Frequency
docs.text:
Medium · String processing extensions · Extension · Learning step 285 of 350

Official LeetCode statement · All Python implementations · Roadmap

Quick review: Frequency maps · Frequency buckets.

docs.title: Task
docs.text: Reorder a string so characters with larger frequencies appear first, with all copies of each character together. Ties may appear in any order.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
1. Count each distinct character before arranging output.
  2. Frequencies lie between one and n, so they can serve as bucket indices.
Show approaches, complexity comparison, proofs, and Python solutions

Previous: 284 · #443 · Next: 286 · #609

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Frequency buckets O(n+u) O(n+u), including output Sorted frequency entries O(n+u log u) O(n+u) including output; O(u) other storage

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Frequency buckets
docs.text: Count characters, place each distinct character into the bucket indexed by its count, then read buckets from n down to one. Emit each character repeated by its bucket index.

docs.title: Sorted frequency entries
docs.text: Sort the distinct (character, count) pairs by descending count. Emit one block per sorted entry. This avoids n bucket objects when only a few symbols occur.

docs.title: Why it works
docs.text: Each character is counted once and emitted exactly that many times, preserving the input multiset. Descending bucket indices and descending sorted counts both ensure that no lower-frequency block precedes a higher-frequency block. Tie order does not affect validity, so no secondary comparison is necessary.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For "banana", the counts are a:3, n:2, b:1. Both versions return "aaannb". For equal counts, several results are valid; tests should check the contract rather than requiring a particular incidental dictionary order.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text: Let n be input length and u distinct symbols. Buckets take O(n+u) time and O(n+u) space. Sorting entries takes O(n+u log u) time and O(n+u) space including output. Its non-output storage is O(u), unlike the O(n+u) bucket allocation. The given alphabet bounds u, but retaining u makes the tradeoff explicit. Joining prebuilt blocks is linear in output size. The input string is unchanged.

docs.title: Python implementations
docs.text: Each code block is independent and uses the canonical LeetCode class name. Choose one block to paste into the Python3 editor. Shared node definitions are included where needed.

docs.title: 1. Frequency buckets
docs.text:
Time: O(n+u)

Space: O(n+u), including output

from collections import Counter


class Solution:
    """Approach: Frequency buckets
    Time: O(n+u)
    Space: O(n+u), including output
    """

    def frequencySort(self, s: str) -> str:
        counts = Counter(s)
        buckets = [[] for _ in range(len(s) + 1)]
        for char, count in counts.items():
            buckets[count].append(char)
        return "".join(char * count for count in range(len(s), 0, -1) for char in buckets[count])

docs.title: 2. Sorted frequency entries
docs.text:
Time: O(n+u log u)

Space: O(n+u) including output; O(u) other storage

from collections import Counter


class Solution:
    """Approach: Sorted frequency entries
    Time: O(n+u log u)
    Space: O(n+u) including output; O(u) other storage
    """

    def frequencySort(self, s: str) -> str:
        entries = sorted(Counter(s).items(), key=lambda item: -item[1])
        return "".join(char * count for char, count in entries)

docs.text:

docs.title: Task
docs.text: Each closed interval describes a balloon. An arrow at x bursts every balloon whose interval contains x. Return the minimum arrows.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
1. Shoot at the earliest ending remaining interval.
  2. Overlapping balloon groups can also be tracked by their common intersection.

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Earliest-end arrow placement O(n log n) O(n) Start-order intersection groups O(n log n) O(n)

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Earliest-end arrow placement
docs.text: Sort by right endpoint. Place a new arrow at an interval end only when the preceding arrow lies before its start.

docs.title: Start-order intersection groups
docs.text: Sort by start and maintain the right edge of the common intersection. A disjoint new interval closes one arrow group.

docs.title: Earliest-end arrow placement
docs.text: Any arrow bursting the earliest-ending balloon can be moved to its right endpoint without losing any other currently intersected balloon. Repeating this exchange yields an optimal greedy assignment.

docs.title: Start-order intersection groups
docs.text: All intervals in a group share the maintained intersection, so one arrow suffices. A new start beyond that intersection requires a second arrow in every assignment, justifying the group split.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: [[10,16],[2,8],[1,6],[7,12]] can be burst at x=6 and x=12, for two arrows.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text:
Earliest-end arrow placement: O(n log n) time; O(n) space.

Start-order intersection groups: O(n log n) time; O(n) space.

Inputs are unchanged. Intervals are closed: touching endpoints share an arrow, unlike the compatibility rule for non-overlapping half-open intervals.

docs.title: 1. Earliest-end arrow placement

Time: O(n log n)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Earliest-end arrow placement
    Time: O(n log n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def findMinArrowShots(self, points: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        arrows = 0
        position = float("-inf")
        for start, end in sorted(points, key=lambda point: point[1]):
            if start > position:
                arrows += 1
                position = end
        return arrows

docs.title: 2. Start-order intersection groups
docs.text:
Time: O(n log n)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Start-order intersection groups
    Time: O(n log n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def findMinArrowShots(self, points: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        end = float("-inf")
        arrows = 0
        for start, finish in sorted(points):
            if start > end:
                arrows += 1
                end = finish
            else:
                end = min(end, finish)
        return arrows

docs.title: Hash pair-sum frequencies

Space: O(n squared)

from collections import Counter


class Solution:
    """Approach: Hash pair-sum frequencies
    Time: O(n squared) expected
    Space: O(n squared)
    """

    def fourSumCount(self, nums1, nums2, nums3, nums4) -> int:
        counts = Counter(a + b for a in nums1 for b in nums2)
        return sum(counts[-c - d] for c in nums3 for d in nums4)

docs.title: 2. Sorted pair sums with run counting
docs.text:
Time: O(n squared log n)

Space: O(n squared)

from collections import Counter


class Solution:
    """Approach: Sorted pair sums with run counting
    Time: O(n squared log n)
    Space: O(n squared)
    """

    def fourSumCount(self, nums1, nums2, nums3, nums4) -> int:
        left = sorted(a + b for a in nums1 for b in nums2)
        right = sorted(c + d for c in nums3 for d in nums4)
        i, j, answer = 0, len(right) - 1, 0
        while i < len(left) and j >= 0:
            total = left[i] + right[j]
            if total < 0:
                i += 1
            elif total > 0:
                j -= 1
            else:
                start, end = i, j
                a, b = left[i], right[j]
                while i < len(left) and left[i] == a:
                    i += 1
                while j >= 0 and right[j] == b:
                    j -= 1
                answer += (i - start) * (end - j)
        return answer

docs.title: Reverse monotonic stack
docs.text: Scan from right to left with a decreasing stack and the largest confirmed third value. A larger incoming value pops possible third values; any later smaller incoming value completes the pattern.

docs.title: Prefix minima with sorted suffix
docs.text: Try each middle index using the minimum prefix value and a sorted multiset of later values. Binary-search for a suffix value strictly between the two. List removals make this an educational baseline that may time out.

docs.title: Reverse monotonic stack
docs.text: Every saved third value has a larger second value earlier than it in the processed suffix. If the current value is smaller, the index and value orders both hold. Popping records the best third value without losing any future witness.

docs.title: Prefix minima with sorted suffix
docs.text: For a chosen middle index, a witness exists exactly when a later value is greater than the smallest preceding value and smaller than the middle value. Lower bound finds the smallest eligible later value.

docs.title: Walkthrough

from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Reverse monotonic stack
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def find132pattern(self, nums: list[int]) -> bool:
        stack = []
        third = float("-inf")
        for value in reversed(nums):
            if value < third:
                return True
            while stack and stack[-1] < value:
                third = stack.pop()
            stack.append(value)
        return False

docs.title: 2. Prefix minima with sorted suffix
docs.text:
Time: O(n squared)

Space: O(n)

from bisect import bisect_left, bisect_right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Prefix minima with sorted suffix
    Time: O(n squared)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def find132pattern(self, nums: list[int]) -> bool:
        if len(nums) < 3:
            return False
        suffix = sorted(nums[1:])
        smallest = nums[0]
        for j in range(1, len(nums) - 1):
            suffix.pop(bisect_left(suffix, nums[j]))
            index = bisect_right(suffix, smallest)
            if index < len(suffix) and suffix[index] < nums[j]:
                return True
            smallest = min(smallest, nums[j])
        return False

docs.title: Timestamped entries and eviction scan
docs.text: Store value, frequency, and last-use timestamp per key. When full, scan for the lexicographically smallest (frequency,timestamp) victim.

docs.title: Frequency buckets with ordered recency
docs.text: Buckets partition live keys by exact frequency; their order records tie-breaking last use. Moving a touched key updates both invariants, and minimum-frequency oldest eviction follows the required policy.

docs.title: Timestamped entries and eviction scan

docs.title: 1. Frequency buckets with ordered recency
docs.text:
Time: O(1) expected per operation

Space: O(capacity)

from collections import OrderedDict


class LFUCache:
    """Approach: Frequency buckets with ordered recency
    Time: O(1) expected per operation
    Space: O(capacity)
    """

    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.values = {}
        self.buckets = {}
        self.minimum = 0

    def _touch(self, key):
        value, frequency = self.values[key]
        bucket = self.buckets[frequency]
        del bucket[key]
        if not bucket:
            del self.buckets[frequency]
            if self.minimum == frequency:
                self.minimum += 1
        frequency += 1
        self.values[key] = (value, frequency)
        self.buckets.setdefault(frequency, OrderedDict())[key] = None
        return value

    def get(self, key: int) -> int:
        return self._touch(key) if key in self.values else -1

    def put(self, key: int, value: int) -> None:
        if self.capacity == 0:
            return
        if key in self.values:
            self.values[key] = (value, self.values[key][1])
            self._touch(key)
            return
        if len(self.values) == self.capacity:
            bucket = self.buckets[self.minimum]
            victim, _ = bucket.popitem(last=False)
            del self.values[victim]
            if not bucket:
                del self.buckets[self.minimum]
        self.values[key] = (value, 1)
        self.buckets.setdefault(1, OrderedDict())[key] = None
        self.minimum = 1

docs.title: 2. Timestamped entries and eviction scan
docs.text:
Time: O(1) get/update; O(capacity) eviction; misses required O(1)

Space: O(capacity)

from collections import OrderedDict


class LFUCache:
    """Approach: Timestamped entries and eviction scan
    Time: O(1) get/update; O(capacity) eviction; misses required O(1)
    Space: O(capacity)
    """

    def __init__(self, capacity: int):
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.clock = 0
        self.entries = {}

    def get(self, key: int) -> int:
        if key not in self.entries:
            return -1
        self.clock += 1
        value, frequency, _ = self.entries[key]
        self.entries[key] = (value, frequency + 1, self.clock)
        return value

    def put(self, key: int, value: int) -> None:
        if self.capacity == 0:
            return
        self.clock += 1
        if key in self.entries:
            frequency = self.entries[key][1] + 1
        else:
            frequency = 1
            if len(self.entries) == self.capacity:
                victim = min(self.entries, key=lambda candidate: self.entries[candidate][1:])
                del self.entries[victim]
        self.entries[key] = (value, frequency, self.clock)

Approach Time Space Memoized chosen-mask minimax O(M*2^M) O(2^M) Descending-mask retrograde game table O(M*2^M) O(2^M)

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Memoized chosen-mask minimax
docs.text: Cache chosen masks and their implied remaining target. Try each unused choice and return true if it wins now or gives the opponent a losing continuation.

docs.title: Descending-mask retrograde game table
docs.text: Precompute selected-value totals for all masks, then fill winning states in decreasing numeric mask order. Any move adds a bit, reaching an already solved larger mask.

docs.title: Memoized chosen-mask minimax
docs.text: This is the definition of a forced win in a finite alternating game: one winning move suffices, while a state with only opponent-winning continuations loses. The mask uniquely determines needed, so the cache has at most 2^M meaningful states.

docs.title: Descending-mask retrograde game table
docs.text: A terminal-reaching move wins immediately; every other move is good exactly when its successor is losing. Descending-mask order respects these dependencies and evaluates the same exhaustive game condition without recursion.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: With choices 1..10 and target 11, every first choice can be answered by its complement to 11, so the first player loses.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text:
Memoized chosen-mask minimax: O(M2^M) time; O(2^M) space. Descending-mask retrograde game table: O(M2^M) time; O(2^M) space.

M<=20. Both preserve inputs and first reject globally unreachable targets; target zero is already satisfied. Memo recursion depth is bounded by M, while the dense variant always allocates two 2^M arrays and may do substantially more work.

docs.text:
Time: O(M*2^M)

Space: O(2^M)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Memoized chosen-mask minimax
    Time: O(M*2^M)
    Space: O(2^M)
    """

    def canIWin(self, maxChoosableInteger: int, desiredTotal: int) -> bool:
        from functools import cache

        maximum = maxChoosableInteger
        if desiredTotal <= 0:
            return True
        if maximum * (maximum + 1) // 2 < desiredTotal:
            return False

        @cache
        def winning(mask, needed):
            for value in range(1, maximum + 1):
                bit = 1 << (value - 1)
                if not mask & bit and (value >= needed or not winning(mask | bit, needed - value)):
                    return True
            return False

        return winning(0, desiredTotal)

docs.title: 2. Descending-mask retrograde game table
docs.text:
Time: O(M*2^M)

Space: O(2^M)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Descending-mask retrograde game table
    Time: O(M*2^M)
    Space: O(2^M)
    """

    def canIWin(self, maxChoosableInteger: int, desiredTotal: int) -> bool:
        maximum = maxChoosableInteger
        if desiredTotal <= 0:
            return True
        if maximum * (maximum + 1) // 2 < desiredTotal:
            return False
        size = 1 << maximum
        totals = [0] * size
        for mask in range(1, size):
            bit = mask & -mask
            totals[mask] = totals[mask ^ bit] + bit.bit_length()
        wins = [False] * size
        for mask in range(size - 1, -1, -1):
            if totals[mask] >= desiredTotal:
                continue
            for value in range(1, maximum + 1):
                bit = 1 << (value - 1)
                if not mask & bit and (
                    totals[mask] + value >= desiredTotal or not wins[mask | bit]
                ):
                    wins[mask] = True
                    break
        return wins[0]

docs.text: Scan backward and retain the longest valid run beginning with each letter. Sum all represented prefix lengths.

docs.title: Longest valid run per ending letter
docs.text: A wraparound substring is uniquely determined by its final letter and length. An observed run of length L supplies every length 1 through L for that letter, so the maximum represents exactly its distinct possibilities.

docs.title: Longest valid run per starting letter

class Solution:
    """Approach: Longest valid run per ending letter
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(26)
    """

    def findSubstringInWraproundString(self, s: str) -> int:
        best = [0] * 26
        run = 0
        for index, character in enumerate(s):
            run = run + 1 if index and (ord(character) - ord(s[index - 1])) % 26 == 1 else 1
            letter = ord(character) - ord("a")
            best[letter] = max(best[letter], run)
        return sum(best)

    Time: O(n)

        best = [0] * 26
        run = 0
        for index in range(len(s) - 1, -1, -1):
            run = (
                run + 1
                if index + 1 < len(s) and (ord(s[index + 1]) - ord(s[index])) % 26 == 1
                else 1
            )
            letter = ord(s[index]) - ord("a")
            best[letter] = max(best[letter], run)
        return sum(best)

docs.title: Descending bucket assignment
docs.text: Sort a copy descending and place each next value into a bucket that stays within the target. Skip buckets with a load already tried at this depth; stop after a failed empty bucket.

docs.title: Used-mask remainder DP
docs.text: For each reachable index mask store the current unfinished bucket sum. Add an unused value if it fits; a completed bucket resets the remainder to zero.

docs.title: Descending bucket assignment

Exponential search is appropriate for the small maximum n (15 or 16). Sorting largest first exposes impossible assignments earlier. The bitmask table trades predictable work for exponential storage.

docs.title: 1. Descending bucket assignment
docs.text:
Time: O(n log n + k^n) loose bound

Space: O(n+k)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Descending bucket assignment
    Time: O(n log n + k^n) loose bound
    Space: O(n+k)
    """

    def makesquare(self, matchsticks: list[int]) -> bool:
        k = 4
        values = sorted(matchsticks, reverse=True)
        total = sum(values)
        if total % k:
            return False
        target = total // k
        if values[0] > target:
            return False
        loads = [0] * k

        def place(index):
            if index == len(values):
                return True
            tried = set()
            for bucket, load in enumerate(loads):
                if load in tried or load + values[index] > target:
                    continue
                tried.add(load)
                loads[bucket] += values[index]
                if place(index + 1):
                    return True
                loads[bucket] -= values[index]
                if load == 0:
                    break
            return False

        return place(0)

docs.title: 2. Used-mask remainder DP
docs.text:
Time: O(n*2^n)

Space: O(2^n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Used-mask remainder DP
    Time: O(n*2^n)
    Space: O(2^n)
    """

    def makesquare(self, matchsticks: list[int]) -> bool:
        k = 4
        values = matchsticks
        total = sum(values)
        if total % k:
            return False
        target = total // k
        if target == 0:
            return True
        remainders = [-1] * (1 << len(values))
        remainders[0] = 0
        for mask, remainder in enumerate(remainders):
            if remainder < 0:
                continue
            for index, value in enumerate(values):
                bit = 1 << index
                if not mask & bit and remainder + value <= target:
                    remainders[mask | bit] = (remainder + value) % target
        return remainders[-1] == 0

class Solution:
    """Approach: Per-bit population counts
    Time: O(30n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def totalHammingDistance(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        answer = 0
        for bit in range(30):
            ones = sum((value >> bit) & 1 for value in nums)
            answer += ones * (len(nums) - ones)
        return answer

class Solution:
    """Approach: Direct XOR pair enumeration
    Time: O(n squared)
    Space: O(1)

        answer = 0
        for i, value in enumerate(nums):
            for j in range(i + 1, len(nums)):
                answer += (value ^ nums[j]).bit_count()
        return answer

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Rolling interval score differences
    Time: O(n^2)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def predictTheWinner(self, nums: list[int]) -> bool:
        dp = nums.copy()
        for left in range(len(nums) - 2, -1, -1):
            for right in range(left + 1, len(nums)):
                dp[right] = max(nums[left] - dp[right], nums[right] - dp[right - 1])
        return dp[-1] >= 0

class Solution:
    """Approach: Absolute best score and interval totals
    Time: O(n^2)
    Space: O(n^2)
    """

    def predictTheWinner(self, nums: list[int]) -> bool:
        prefix = [0]
        for value in nums:
            prefix.append(prefix[-1] + value)
        dp = [[0] * len(nums) for _ in nums]
        for left in range(len(nums) - 1, -1, -1):
            dp[left][left] = nums[left]
            for right in range(left + 1, len(nums)):
                total = prefix[right + 1] - prefix[left]
                dp[left][right] = total - min(dp[left + 1][right], dp[left][right - 1])
        return 2 * dp[0][-1] >= prefix[-1]

Space: O(S)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Signed-sum frequency frontier
    Time: O(n*S)
    Space: O(S)
    """

    def findTargetSumWays(self, nums: list[int], target: int) -> int:
        counts = {0: 1}
        for value in nums:
            following = {}
            for total, count in counts.items():
                for signed in (total + value, total - value):
                    following[signed] = following.get(signed, 0) + count
            counts = following
        return counts.get(target, 0)

docs.title: 2. Negative-subset count DP
docs.text:
Time: O(n*S)

Space: O(S)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Negative-subset count DP
    Time: O(n*S)
    Space: O(S)
    """

    def findTargetSumWays(self, nums: list[int], target: int) -> int:
        total = sum(nums)
        if abs(target) > total or (total - target) % 2:
            return 0
        goal = (total - target) // 2
        dp = [0] * (goal + 1)
        dp[0] = 1
        for value in nums:
            for subtotal in range(goal, value - 1, -1):
                dp[subtotal] += dp[subtotal - value]
        return dp[goal]

class Solution:
    """Approach: Diagonal coordinate bounds
    Time: O(mn)
    Space: O(1) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def findDiagonalOrder(self, mat: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        rows, cols = len(mat), len(mat[0])
        answer = []
        for diagonal in range(rows + cols - 1):
            low, high = max(0, diagonal - cols + 1), min(rows - 1, diagonal)
            indices = range(high, low - 1, -1) if diagonal % 2 == 0 else range(low, high + 1)
            for row in indices:
                answer.append(mat[row][diagonal - row])
        return answer

Space: O(mn)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Group cells by diagonal
    Time: O(mn)
    Space: O(mn)
    """

    def findDiagonalOrder(self, mat: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        buckets = [[] for _ in range(len(mat) + len(mat[0]) - 1)]
        for row, values in enumerate(mat):
            for col, value in enumerate(values):
                buckets[row + col].append(value)
        answer = []
        for diagonal, values in enumerate(buckets):
            answer.extend(reversed(values) if diagonal % 2 == 0 else values)
        return answer

Neither variant changes the tree. n is node count, h height, and w maximum occupied width. Both are iterative, so a deep chain does not exceed Python recursion depth. Negative values remain valid.

docs.title: 1. Breadth-first row processing
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(w) auxiliary plus output

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Breadth-first row processing
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(w) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def findBottomLeftValue(self, root: TreeNode) -> int:
        queue = deque([root])
        answer = root.val
        while queue:
            answer = queue[0].val
            for _ in range(len(queue)):
                node = queue.popleft()
                if node.left:
                    queue.append(node.left)
                if node.right:
                    queue.append(node.right)
        return answer

docs.title: 2. Depth-indexed iterative DFS
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(h) auxiliary plus output

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Depth-indexed iterative DFS
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def findBottomLeftValue(self, root: TreeNode) -> int:
        stack = [(root, 0)]
        deepest = -1
        answer = root.val
        while stack:
            node, depth = stack.pop()
            if depth > deepest:
                deepest, answer = depth, node.val
            if node.right:
                stack.append((node.right, depth + 1))
            if node.left:
                stack.append((node.left, depth + 1))
        return answer

docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(w) auxiliary plus output

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Breadth-first row processing
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(w) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def largestValues(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> list[int]:
        result = []
        queue = deque([root]) if root else deque()
        while queue:
            maximum = float("-inf")
            for _ in range(len(queue)):
                node = queue.popleft()
                maximum = max(maximum, node.val)
                if node.left:
                    queue.append(node.left)
                if node.right:
                    queue.append(node.right)
            result.append(maximum)
        return result

docs.title: 2. Depth-indexed iterative DFS
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(h) auxiliary plus output

from collections import deque


class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val=0, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


class Solution:
    """Approach: Depth-indexed iterative DFS
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(h) auxiliary plus output
    """

    def largestValues(self, root: TreeNode | None) -> list[int]:
        result = []
        stack = [(root, 0)] if root else []
        while stack:
            node, depth = stack.pop()
            if depth == len(result):
                result.append(node.val)
            else:
                result[depth] = max(result[depth], node.val)
            for child in (node.left, node.right):
                if child:
                    stack.append((child, depth + 1))
        return result

docs.title: Interval palindrome table
docs.text: An optimal palindrome can use both equal endpoints around an optimal interior. If endpoints differ they cannot both be used as the outside pair, so at least one must be omitted.

docs.title: LCS against the reversed string
docs.text: Every palindromic subsequence is common to both strings. Conversely, a longest common subsequence can be symmetrized around the crossing of forward and reverse positions without reducing its length, giving an equally long palindrome. This equivalence is for length; arbitrary LCS reconstruction need not itself be palindromic.

Space: O(n^2)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Interval palindrome table
    Time: O(n^2)
    Space: O(n^2)
    """

    def longestPalindromeSubseq(self, s: str) -> int:
        dp = [[0] * len(s) for _ in s]
        for left in range(len(s) - 1, -1, -1):
            dp[left][left] = 1
            for right in range(left + 1, len(s)):
                dp[left][right] = (
                    2 + dp[left + 1][right - 1]
                    if s[left] == s[right]
                    else max(dp[left + 1][right], dp[left][right - 1])
                )
        return dp[0][-1]

docs.title: 2. LCS against the reversed string
docs.text:
Time: O(n^2)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: LCS against the reversed string
    Time: O(n^2)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def longestPalindromeSubseq(self, s: str) -> int:
        reverse = s[::-1]
        dp = [0] * (len(s) + 1)
        for first in s:
            diagonal = 0
            for column, second in enumerate(reverse, 1):
                above = dp[column]
                dp[column] = diagonal + 1 if first == second else max(above, dp[column - 1])
                diagonal = above
        return dp[-1]

class Solution:
    """Approach: Denomination-first rolling counts
    Time: O(C*A)
    Space: O(A)
    """

    def change(self, amount: int, coins: list[int]) -> int:
        dp = [0] * (amount + 1)
        dp[0] = 1
        for coin in coins:
            for total in range(coin, amount + 1):
                dp[total] += dp[total - coin]
        return dp[amount]

Space: O(C*A+C+A)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Coin-prefix and amount table
    Time: O(C*A)
    Space: O(C*A+C+A)
    """

    def change(self, amount: int, coins: list[int]) -> int:
        dp = [[0] * (amount + 1) for _ in range(len(coins) + 1)]
        dp[0][0] = 1
        for count, coin in enumerate(coins, 1):
            for total in range(amount + 1):
                dp[count][total] = dp[count - 1][total]
                if total >= coin:
                    dp[count][total] += dp[count][total - coin]
        return dp[-1][-1]

docs.title: Earliest index per remainder
docs.text: Equal remainders mean the difference of prefix sums is divisible by k. The earliest matching index gives the longest available gap, so rejecting shorter matches loses no valid answer.

docs.title: Delayed prefix-remainder set

docs.title: 1. Earliest index per remainder
docs.text:
Time: O(n) expected

Space: O(min(n,k))

class Solution:
    """Approach: Earliest index per remainder
    Time: O(n) expected
    Space: O(min(n,k))
    """

    def checkSubarraySum(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> bool:
        first = {0: -1}
        remainder = 0
        for i, value in enumerate(nums):
            remainder = (remainder + value) % k
            if remainder in first:
                if i - first[remainder] >= 2:
                    return True
            else:
                first[remainder] = i
        return False

docs.title: 2. Delayed prefix-remainder set
docs.text:
Time: O(n) expected

Space: O(min(n,k))

class Solution:
    """Approach: Delayed prefix-remainder set
    Time: O(n) expected
    Space: O(min(n,k))
    """

    def checkSubarraySum(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> bool:
        eligible = set()
        previous = current = 0
        for value in nums:
            current = (current + value) % k
            if current in eligible:
                return True
            eligible.add(previous)
            previous = current
        return False

docs.text: Equal prefix balances mean the interval has net balance zero, hence equal counts. The earliest occurrence gives the longest interval ending at the current index, so later occurrences must never replace it.

docs.title: Sort equal prefix balances
docs.text: A subarray is balanced exactly when its endpoint prefix balances match. The farthest pair in each group is its longest candidate; taking the largest group span is optimal.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For [0, 0, 1, 1, 1], balances are -1, -2, -1, 0, 1. Balance 0 was first seen at index -1; repeating it at index 3 gives length 4.

Default approach (First index per balance):

Expected O(n) time and O(n) space. Inputs are unchanged. Seed balance 0 at -1 to include intervals starting at index 0. This problem stores an earliest index, unlike Subarray Sum Equals K, which needs a count of earlier prefixes.

First index per balance: O(n) expected time; O(n) space. Sort equal prefix balances: O(n log n) time; O(n) space. Pair every prefix balance with its index, sort the pairs, and compare the smallest and largest index in each equal-balance group. This replaces hashing with sorting.

class Solution:
    """Approach: First index per balance
    Time: O(n) expected
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def findMaxLength(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        first = {0: -1}
        balance = best = 0
        for i, number in enumerate(nums):
            balance += 1 if number else -1
            if balance in first:
                best = max(best, i - first[balance])
            else:
                first[balance] = i
        return best

docs.text:
Time: O(n log n)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Sort equal prefix balances
    Time: O(n log n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def findMaxLength(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        prefixes = [(0, -1)]
        balance = 0
        for i, value in enumerate(nums):
            balance += 1 if value else -1
            prefixes.append((balance, i))
        prefixes.sort()
        first = 0
        best = 0
        for i, (balance, index) in enumerate(prefixes):
            if i == 0 or balance != prefixes[i - 1][0]:
                first = index
            best = max(best, index - first)
        return best

class Solution:
    """Approach: Even-pair boundary binary search
    Time: O(log n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def singleNonDuplicate(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        low, high = 0, len(nums) - 1
        while low < high:
            middle = (low + high) // 2
            middle -= middle % 2
            if nums[middle] == nums[middle + 1]:
                low = middle + 2
            else:
                high = middle
        return nums[low]

        answer = 0
        for value in nums:
            answer ^= value
        return answer

docs.text:
Time: O(R*C)

Space: O(R*C)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Multi-source zero BFS
    Time: O(R*C)
    Space: O(R*C)
    """

    def updateMatrix(self, mat: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
        from collections import deque

        rows, columns = len(mat), len(mat[0])
        distance = [[-1] * columns for _ in range(rows)]
        queue = deque()
        for r in range(rows):
            for c in range(columns):
                if mat[r][c] == 0:
                    distance[r][c] = 0
                    queue.append((r, c))
        while queue:
            r, c = queue.popleft()
            for nr, nc in ((r - 1, c), (r + 1, c), (r, c - 1), (r, c + 1)):
                if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < columns and distance[nr][nc] < 0:
                    distance[nr][nc] = distance[r][c] + 1
                    queue.append((nr, nc))
        return distance

docs.title: 2. Forward and backward distance sweeps
docs.text:
Time: O(R*C)

Space: O(R*C)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Forward and backward distance sweeps
    Time: O(R*C)
    Space: O(R*C)
    """

    def updateMatrix(self, mat: list[list[int]]) -> list[list[int]]:
        rows, columns = len(mat), len(mat[0])
        distance = [[0 if value == 0 else rows + columns for value in row] for row in mat]
        for r in range(rows):
            for c in range(columns):
                if r:
                    distance[r][c] = min(distance[r][c], distance[r - 1][c] + 1)
                if c:
                    distance[r][c] = min(distance[r][c], distance[r][c - 1] + 1)
        for r in range(rows - 1, -1, -1):
            for c in range(columns - 1, -1, -1):
                if r + 1 < rows:
                    distance[r][c] = min(distance[r][c], distance[r + 1][c] + 1)
                if c + 1 < columns:
                    distance[r][c] = min(distance[r][c], distance[r][c + 1] + 1)
        return distance

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Iterative adjacency-matrix DFS
    Time: O(n^2)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def findCircleNum(self, isConnected: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        seen = set()
        count = 0
        for start in range(len(isConnected)):
            if start in seen:
                continue
            count += 1
            seen.add(start)
            stack = [start]
            while stack:
                node = stack.pop()
                for other, connected in enumerate(isConnected[node]):
                    if connected and other not in seen:
                        seen.add(other)
                        stack.append(other)
        return count

docs.title: 2. Union the upper matrix triangle
docs.text:
Time: O(n^2*alpha(n))

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Union the upper matrix triangle
    Time: O(n^2*alpha(n))
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def findCircleNum(self, isConnected: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        n = len(isConnected)
        parent, size = list(range(n)), [1] * n

        def find(node):
            while parent[node] != node:
                parent[node] = parent[parent[node]]
                node = parent[node]
            return node

        count = n
        for a in range(n):
            for b in range(a + 1, n):
                if isConnected[a][b]:
                    ra, rb = find(a), find(b)
                    if ra != rb:
                        if size[ra] < size[rb]:
                            ra, rb = rb, ra
                        parent[rb] = ra
                        size[ra] += size[rb]
                        count -= 1
        return count

docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(1)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Six rolling attendance states
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def checkRecord(self, n: int) -> int:
        modulus = 1_000_000_007
        counts = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 0, 0]]
        for _ in range(n):
            following = [[0] * 3 for _ in range(2)]
            for absences in range(2):
                for late in range(3):
                    count = counts[absences][late]
                    following[absences][0] = (following[absences][0] + count) % modulus
                    if absences == 0:
                        following[1][0] = (following[1][0] + count) % modulus
                    if late < 2:
                        following[absences][late + 1] = (
                            following[absences][late + 1] + count
                        ) % modulus
            counts = following
        return sum(map(sum, counts)) % modulus

docs.title: 2. Six-state transition exponentiation
docs.text:
Time: O(6^3*log n)

Space: O(6^2)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Six-state transition exponentiation
    Time: O(6^3*log n)
    Space: O(6^2)
    """

    def checkRecord(self, n: int) -> int:
        modulus = 1_000_000_007
        transition = [[0] * 6 for _ in range(6)]
        for absences in range(2):
            for late in range(3):
                source = absences * 3 + late
                transition[absences * 3][source] += 1
                if absences == 0:
                    transition[3][source] += 1
                if late < 2:
                    transition[source + 1][source] += 1
        counts = [1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]

        def square(matrix):
            return [
                [sum(matrix[r][k] * matrix[k][c] for k in range(6)) % modulus for c in range(6)]
                for r in range(6)
            ]

        power = n
        while power:
            if power & 1:
                counts = [
                    sum(transition[r][c] * counts[c] for c in range(6)) % modulus for r in range(6)
                ]
            transition = square(transition)
            power >>= 1
        return sum(counts) % modulus

class Solution:
    """Approach: Online prefix frequencies
    Time: O(n) expected
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def subarraySum(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        frequencies = {0: 1}
        prefix = result = 0
        for number in nums:
            prefix += number
            result += frequencies.get(prefix - k, 0)
            frequencies[prefix] = frequencies.get(prefix, 0) + 1
        return result

            for end in range(start, len(nums)):
                total += nums[end]
                answer += total == k
        return answer

Space: O(26)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Fixed frequency-vector window
    Time: O(26n)
    Space: O(26)
    """

    def checkInclusion(self, s1: str, s2: str) -> bool:
        width = len(s1)
        if width > len(s2):
            return False
        need, window = [0] * 26, [0] * 26
        for char in s1:
            need[ord(char) - ord("a")] += 1
        for right, char in enumerate(s2):
            window[ord(char) - ord("a")] += 1
            if right >= width:
                window[ord(s2[right - width]) - ord("a")] -= 1
            if right >= width - 1 and window == need:
                return True
        return False

docs.title: 2. Deficit-count window
docs.text:
Time: O(n+m) expected

Space: O(alphabet)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Deficit-count window
    Time: O(n+m) expected
    Space: O(alphabet)
    """

    def checkInclusion(self, s1: str, s2: str) -> bool:
        need = {}
        for char in s1:
            need[char] = need.get(char, 0) + 1
        missing = len(s1)
        left = 0
        for right, char in enumerate(s2):
            if need.get(char, 0) > 0:
                missing -= 1
            need[char] = need.get(char, 0) - 1
            if right - left + 1 > len(s1):
                outgoing = s2[left]
                need[outgoing] = need.get(outgoing, 0) + 1
                if need[outgoing] > 0:
                    missing += 1
                left += 1
            if right - left + 1 == len(s1) and missing == 0:
                return True
        return False

docs.title: Forward in-grid path-count layers
docs.text: Start with one path at the source. Send each layer count to four neighbors; collect out-of-grid contributions immediately and propagate only inside states.

docs.title: Memoized remaining-move exits
docs.text: Memoize the number of exit completions from a cell with a remaining budget. An already-outside state contributes one; an inside state with no moves contributes zero.

docs.title: Forward in-grid path-count layers
docs.text: Each path is classified by its last step. A path is counted exactly once on its first exit, and exited paths are never extended, so summing all layers counts precisely exits within the move budget.

docs.title: Memoized remaining-move exits
docs.text: The next direction partitions every possible exit path into four disjoint choices. Outside states terminate before the budget-zero test, so an exit on the final allowed step is included.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: On a 1x1 grid with one move, all four directions leave the grid, giving 4.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text:
Forward in-grid path-count layers: O((M+1)RC) time; O(R*C) space. Memoized remaining-move exits: O((M+1)RC) time; O((M+1)RC) space.

M=maxMove, R=m, C=n. No inputs are mutated. Memo recursion is bounded by maxMove<=50; its cache includes move count, while the forward default retains only two grid layers. Zero moves returns zero.

docs.text:
Time: O((M+1)RC)

Space: O(R*C)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Forward in-grid path-count layers
    Time: O((M+1)*R*C)
    Space: O(R*C)
    """

    def findPaths(self, m: int, n: int, maxMove: int, startRow: int, startColumn: int) -> int:
        modulus = 1_000_000_007
        current = [[0] * n for _ in range(m)]
        current[startRow][startColumn] = 1
        answer = 0
        for _ in range(maxMove):
            following = [[0] * n for _ in range(m)]
            for r in range(m):
                for c in range(n):
                    count = current[r][c]
                    for nr, nc in ((r - 1, c), (r + 1, c), (r, c - 1), (r, c + 1)):
                        if 0 <= nr < m and 0 <= nc < n:
                            following[nr][nc] = (following[nr][nc] + count) % modulus
                        else:
                            answer = (answer + count) % modulus
            current = following
        return answer

docs.title: 2. Memoized remaining-move exits
docs.text:
Time: O((M+1)RC)

Space: O((M+1)RC)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Memoized remaining-move exits
    Time: O((M+1)*R*C)
    Space: O((M+1)*R*C)
    """

    def findPaths(self, m: int, n: int, maxMove: int, startRow: int, startColumn: int) -> int:
        from functools import cache

        modulus = 1_000_000_007

        @cache
        def exits(row, column, remaining):
            if not (0 <= row < m and 0 <= column < n):
                return 1
            if remaining == 0:
                return 0
            return (
                sum(
                    exits(row + dr, column + dc, remaining - 1)
                    for dr, dc in ((1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1), (0, -1))
                )
                % modulus
            )

        return exits(startRow, startColumn, maxMove)

Approach Time Space Content dictionary O(L) expected, including string hashing O(L), including returned paths Sort and group records O(L+fClog f), with f files and longest content C O(L+f), including returned paths

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Content dictionary
docs.text: Parse every record into (content, full path), then append the path to a list under its content key. Return only lists containing at least two paths. Python dictionaries resolve hash collisions using equality, so this does not mistake a hash collision for equal file content.

docs.title: Sort and group records
docs.text: Materialize parsed records and sort by their full content strings. Consecutive equal keys form one group. Keep that group's paths only if it has duplicates. This uses ordering rather than a hash table as the grouping mechanism.

docs.title: Why it works
docs.text: Every parsed file is inserted exactly once. Dictionary equality puts a file in exactly its content-equivalence class. Sorting makes each such class contiguous because equal content keys compare equally. Filtering singleton classes removes precisely the files without duplicates.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For "r a(x) b(y)" and "s c(x)", content x maps to r/a and s/c, while y maps only to r/b. Return [["r/a", "s/c"]]. Equal names in different directories would still be different paths, and different names can have equal content.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text: Let L count parsed content and full-path characters, f be the file count, and C the longest content. Dictionary grouping takes expected O(L) time and O(L) space, including returned paths. Sorting takes O(L+fClog f) worst-case time for lexicographic comparisons and O(L+f) space. These bounds account for string hashing/comparison rather than treating arbitrarily long strings as constant-size keys. Parsing follows the stated no-space record grammar. Inputs are unchanged. This task compares the provided content, not files on disk.

from collections import defaultdict
from itertools import groupby


def _files(paths):
    for entry in paths:
        directory, *records = entry.split()
        for record in records:
            name, _, content = record.partition("(")
            yield content[:-1], directory + "/" + name


class Solution:
    """Approach: Content dictionary
    Time: O(L) expected, including string hashing
    Space: O(L), including returned paths
    """

    def findDuplicate(self, paths: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:
        groups = defaultdict(list)
        for content, path in _files(paths):
            groups[content].append(path)
        return [group for group in groups.values() if len(group) > 1]

docs.title: 2. Sort and group records
docs.text:
Time: O(L+fClog f), with f files and longest content C

Space: O(L+f), including returned paths

from collections import defaultdict
from itertools import groupby


def _files(paths):
    for entry in paths:
        directory, *records = entry.split()
        for record in records:
            name, _, content = record.partition("(")
            yield content[:-1], directory + "/" + name


class Solution:
    """Approach: Sort and group records
    Time: O(L+f*C*log f), with f files and longest content C
    Space: O(L+f), including returned paths
    """

    def findDuplicate(self, paths: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]:
        records = sorted(_files(paths), key=lambda record: record[0])
        answer = []
        for _, group in groupby(records, key=lambda record: record[0]):
            paths_in_group = [path for _, path in group]
            if len(paths_in_group) > 1:
                answer.append(paths_in_group)
        return answer

docs.title: Frequency packing bound
docs.text: The f copies of a most frequent task require f-1 separated blocks; the c final tied tasks occupy the last block tail. Other tasks fill idle slots, and if they overflow the bound, all task slots can be packed without idles.

docs.title: Available-task heap with cooldown queue

from collections import Counter, deque
from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush


class Solution:
    """Approach: Frequency packing bound
    Time: O(T+A)
    Space: O(A)
    """

    def leastInterval(self, tasks: list[str], n: int) -> int:
        counts = Counter(tasks)
        frequency = max(counts.values())
        tied = sum(count == frequency for count in counts.values())
        return max(len(tasks), (frequency - 1) * (n + 1) + tied)

docs.text:
Time: O(T log A)

Space: O(A)

from collections import Counter, deque
from heapq import heapify, heappop, heappush


class Solution:
    """Approach: Available-task heap with cooldown queue
    Time: O(T log A)
    Space: O(A)
    """

    def leastInterval(self, tasks: list[str], n: int) -> int:
        heap = [-count for count in Counter(tasks).values()]
        heapify(heap)
        cooling = deque()
        time = 0
        while heap or cooling:
            if not heap:
                time = max(time, cooling[0][0])
            while cooling and cooling[0][0] <= time:
                _, count = cooling.popleft()
                heappush(heap, count)
            count = heappop(heap) + 1
            time += 1
            if count:
                cooling.append((time + n, count))
        return time

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Fixed circular buffer
docs.text: Allocate k slots and track head plus size. Enqueue writes at (head+size) modulo k; dequeue advances head modulo k.

docs.title: Capacity-limited linked queue
docs.text: Track a singly linked head and tail plus size. Append a new owned node on enqueue and remove the head on dequeue; enforce capacity before allocation.

docs.title: Fixed circular buffer
docs.text: The live entries occupy exactly size consecutive cyclic positions from head. Inserting at the first free position or removing the first live one preserves FIFO order and capacity.

docs.title: Capacity-limited linked queue
docs.text: The chain stores entries in insertion order. Removing only its head implements FIFO, while maintaining size enforces the same fixed-capacity abstract contract without a physical ring.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: At capacity two, enqueue 4 and 7 fills the queue. Dequeue removes 4; enqueue 9 then makes front 7 and rear 9.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text: Fixed circular buffer: O(1) per operation time; O(k) space. Capacity-limited linked queue: O(1) per operation time; O(k) space. Objects own all storage. The linked alternative exposes the same queue API but is not physically circular. After removing its last node, clear both head and tail. The array version uses all k slots because size distinguishes full from empty.

docs.title: 1. Fixed circular buffer
docs.text:
Time: O(1) per operation

Space: O(k)

class QueueNode:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


class MyCircularQueue:
    """Approach: Fixed circular buffer
    Time: O(1) per operation
    Space: O(k)
    """

    def __init__(self, k: int):
        self.values = [0] * k
        self.capacity = k
        self.head = 0
        self.size = 0

    def enQueue(self, value: int) -> bool:
        if self.isFull():
            return False
        self.values[(self.head + self.size) % self.capacity] = value
        self.size += 1
        return True

    def deQueue(self) -> bool:
        if self.isEmpty():
            return False
        self.head = (self.head + 1) % self.capacity
        self.size -= 1
        return True

    def Front(self) -> int:
        return self.values[self.head] if self.size else -1

    def Rear(self) -> int:
        return self.values[(self.head + self.size - 1) % self.capacity] if self.size else -1

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == 0

    def isFull(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == self.capacity

docs.title: 2. Capacity-limited linked queue
docs.text:
Time: O(1) per operation

Space: O(k)

class QueueNode:
    def __init__(self, value):
        self.value = value
        self.next = None


class MyCircularQueue:
    """Approach: Capacity-limited linked queue
    Time: O(1) per operation
    Space: O(k)
    """

    def __init__(self, k: int):
        self.capacity = k
        self.size = 0
        self.head = self.tail = None

    def enQueue(self, value: int) -> bool:
        if self.isFull():
            return False
        node = QueueNode(value)
        if self.tail:
            self.tail.next = node
        else:
            self.head = node
        self.tail = node
        self.size += 1
        return True

    def deQueue(self) -> bool:
        if self.isEmpty():
            return False
        self.head = self.head.next
        self.size -= 1
        if self.head is None:
            self.tail = None
        return True

    def Front(self) -> int:
        return self.head.value if self.head else -1

    def Rear(self) -> int:
        return self.tail.value if self.tail else -1

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == 0

    def isFull(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == self.capacity

docs.title: Head-indexed circular array
docs.text: Track head and size over k fixed slots. Front insertion decrements head; rear insertion writes at head+size. End deletions update head or size.

docs.title: Sentinel doubly linked deque
docs.text: Maintain two sentinels and a live-node count. Insert between the appropriate sentinel and neighbor; delete that end's live node by repairing reciprocal links.

docs.title: Head-indexed circular array
docs.text: The logical deque always occupies size cyclic slots starting at head. Each operation changes exactly its specified end while capacity and emptiness remain explicit.

docs.title: Sentinel doubly linked deque

All operations return status rather than overwrite on overflow. The linked variant implements the same API but is not physically circular. Its empty sentinel chain must remain reciprocal.

docs.title: 1. Head-indexed circular array
docs.text:
Time: O(1) per operation

Space: O(k)

class DequeEntry:
    def __init__(self, value=0):
        self.value = value
        self.previous = self.next = None


class MyCircularDeque:
    """Approach: Head-indexed circular array
    Time: O(1) per operation
    Space: O(k)
    """

    def __init__(self, k: int):
        self.values = [0] * k
        self.capacity, self.head, self.size = k, 0, 0

    def insertFront(self, value: int) -> bool:
        if self.isFull():
            return False
        self.head = (self.head - 1) % self.capacity
        self.values[self.head] = value
        self.size += 1
        return True

    def insertLast(self, value: int) -> bool:
        if self.isFull():
            return False
        self.values[(self.head + self.size) % self.capacity] = value
        self.size += 1
        return True

    def deleteFront(self) -> bool:
        if self.isEmpty():
            return False
        self.head = (self.head + 1) % self.capacity
        self.size -= 1
        return True

    def deleteLast(self) -> bool:
        if self.isEmpty():
            return False
        self.size -= 1
        return True

    def getFront(self) -> int:
        return self.values[self.head] if self.size else -1

    def getRear(self) -> int:
        return self.values[(self.head + self.size - 1) % self.capacity] if self.size else -1

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == 0

    def isFull(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == self.capacity

docs.title: 2. Sentinel doubly linked deque
docs.text:
Time: O(1) per operation

Space: O(k)

class DequeEntry:
    def __init__(self, value=0):
        self.value = value
        self.previous = self.next = None


class MyCircularDeque:
    """Approach: Sentinel doubly linked deque
    Time: O(1) per operation
    Space: O(k)
    """

    def __init__(self, k: int):
        self.capacity, self.size = k, 0
        self.left, self.right = DequeEntry(), DequeEntry()
        self.left.next = self.right
        self.right.previous = self.left

    def _insert(self, before, after, value):
        node = DequeEntry(value)
        node.previous, node.next = before, after
        before.next = after.previous = node
        self.size += 1
        return True

    def _delete(self, node):
        node.previous.next = node.next
        node.next.previous = node.previous
        self.size -= 1
        return True

    def insertFront(self, value: int) -> bool:
        return False if self.isFull() else self._insert(self.left, self.left.next, value)

    def insertLast(self, value: int) -> bool:
        return False if self.isFull() else self._insert(self.right.previous, self.right, value)

    def deleteFront(self) -> bool:
        return False if self.isEmpty() else self._delete(self.left.next)

    def deleteLast(self) -> bool:
        return False if self.isEmpty() else self._delete(self.right.previous)

    def getFront(self) -> int:
        return self.left.next.value if self.size else -1

    def getRear(self) -> int:
        return self.right.previous.value if self.size else -1

    def isEmpty(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == 0

    def isFull(self) -> bool:
        return self.size == self.capacity

docs.title: Earliest-finish interval greedy
docs.text: Sort a copy by finish time and accept each pair whose start exceeds the last accepted finish.

docs.title: All-predecessor pair-chain DP
docs.text: Sort pairs by start and compute the best chain ending at each pair by testing every earlier strictly compatible pair.

docs.title: Earliest-finish interval greedy
docs.text: Replacing the first pair in an optimal remaining chain by an earliest-finishing compatible pair cannot invalidate any later pair. Repeating that exchange proves every greedy acceptance preserves an optimum.

docs.title: All-predecessor pair-chain DP
docs.text: A chain predecessor necessarily starts earlier because each pair starts before its own end. Sorting therefore gives a dependency order, and enumerating all final predecessors produces the exact longest-chain recurrence.

Earliest-finish interval greedy: O(n log n) time; O(n) space. All-predecessor pair-chain DP: O(n^2) time; O(n) space.

Both create a sorted reference list and leave pairs unchanged; that O(n) allocation is included even in the greedy space bound. Touching endpoints do not chain. The quadratic variant trades the exchange proof for an explicit recurrence.

docs.title: 1. Earliest-finish interval greedy
docs.text:

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Earliest-finish interval greedy
    Time: O(n log n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def findLongestChain(self, pairs: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        end = -float("inf")
        answer = 0
        for start, finish in sorted(pairs, key=lambda pair: pair[1]):
            if start > end:
                answer += 1
                end = finish
        return answer

docs.title: 2. All-predecessor pair-chain DP
docs.text:
Time: O(n^2)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: All-predecessor pair-chain DP
    Time: O(n^2)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def findLongestChain(self, pairs: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        ordered = sorted(pairs)
        lengths = [1] * len(ordered)
        for end in range(len(ordered)):
            for previous in range(end):
                if ordered[previous][1] < ordered[end][0]:
                    lengths[end] = max(lengths[end], lengths[previous] + 1)
        return max(lengths)

docs.title: Manacher odd and even radii
docs.text: Maintain separate odd and even radius arrays. Mirror a radius within the rightmost known palindrome, then expand only beyond the guaranteed region.

docs.title: Expand around all centers
docs.text: Every palindrome has one unique center and radius. Expansion visits exactly those endpoint pairs with matching interiors, so every palindrome is counted once.

docs.title: Manacher odd and even radii
docs.text: Reflection supplies a valid radius bounded by the current right edge. Every further successful comparison advances that edge, yielding linear total expansion work. Each radius counts all shorter palindromes with that center.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: For "aaa", three singles, two "aa" substrings, and one "aaa" give 6.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text:
Expand around all centers: O(n^2) time; O(1) space. Manacher odd and even radii: O(n) time; O(n) space.

Inputs are unchanged. Odd radii include the center; even radii count matched pairs across a gap. Counting unique string values would answer a different question.

docs.title: 1. Expand around all centers
docs.text:
Time: O(n^2)

Space: O(1)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Expand around all centers
    Time: O(n^2)
    Space: O(1)
    """

    def countSubstrings(self, s: str) -> int:
        answer = 0
        for center in range(2 * len(s) - 1):
            left, right = center // 2, (center + 1) // 2
            while left >= 0 and right < len(s) and s[left] == s[right]:
                answer += 1
                left -= 1
                right += 1
        return answer

docs.title: 2. Manacher odd and even radii
docs.text:
Time: O(n)

Space: O(n)

class Solution:
    """Approach: Manacher odd and even radii
    Time: O(n)
    Space: O(n)
    """

    def countSubstrings(self, s: str) -> int:
        odd = [0] * len(s)
        left, right = 0, -1
        for i in range(len(s)):
            radius = 1 if i > right else min(odd[left + right - i], right - i + 1)
            while i - radius >= 0 and i + radius < len(s) and s[i - radius] == s[i + radius]:
                radius += 1
            odd[i] = radius
            if i + radius - 1 > right:
                left, right = i - radius + 1, i + radius - 1
        even = [0] * len(s)
        left, right = 0, -1
        for i in range(len(s)):
            radius = 0 if i > right else min(even[left + right - i + 1], right - i + 1)
            while (
                i - radius - 1 >= 0 and i + radius < len(s) and s[i - radius - 1] == s[i + radius]
            ):
                radius += 1
            even[i] = radius
            if i + radius - 1 > right:
                left, right = i - radius, i + radius - 1
        return sum(odd) + sum(even)

docs.title: 648 Replace Words
docs.text:

Official LeetCode statement · All Python implementations · Roadmap

docs.title: Task
docs.text: Replace each word in a sentence by the shortest dictionary root that is its prefix. Leave a word unchanged when no root matches. Preserve word order.

docs.title: Hints
docs.text:
1. The first terminal node reached in a prefix trie is the shortest root.
  2. A simpler comparison strategy checks roots in increasing length order.
Show approaches, complexity comparison, proofs, and Python solutions

Previous: 286 · #609 · Next: 288 · #686

docs.title: Approach comparison
docs.text:
Approach Time Space Prefix trie O(D+L) O(D+L), including split words and output Length-ordered root scan O(R log R+W*D+L); slower dictionary-scan baseline O(R+L), including output

Read each approach's limits and mutation notes below. Educational baselines may exceed a required complexity bound; the default is the first implementation.

docs.title: Prefix trie
docs.text: Insert roots into nested dictionaries with a terminal marker. For each word, walk its characters from the trie root. Stop at the first terminal node, or abandon the search on a missing edge. Slice only the selected replacement.

docs.title: Length-ordered root scan
docs.text: Sort a copy of the dictionary by root length. For each word, choose the first root satisfying startswith. Break early when a root is longer than the word. This avoids a trie but repeatedly compares roots and is a slower learning baseline for large dictionaries and long sentences.

docs.title: Why it works
docs.text: A trie path spells exactly a dictionary prefix. The first terminal along a word's path has the smallest possible length. The sorted scan tests candidate lengths in increasing order, so its first matching root is also shortest. If neither finds a root, no dictionary prefix exists and the original word stays.

docs.title: Walkthrough
docs.text: With roots ["a", "ab", "cat"] and sentence "about cattle dog", the result is "a cat dog". Both a and ab match about, but only the shortest is selected.

docs.title: Cost and pitfalls
docs.text: Let D be total dictionary characters, R its root count, W the number of words, and L the sentence length. Trie construction and replacement take O(D+L) time and O(D+L) space including split words and output. The scan takes O(R log R+W*D+L) worst-case time and O(R+L) extra space. Length sorting uses constant-size keys, but each startswith comparison can inspect its whole root. The dictionary and sentence are unchanged. Check the terminal before trying longer roots; replacing by any matching prefix is not sufficient.
